entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

# Plan: finishing the systems extension (spec §11) in reviewed milestones

Status: DRAFT (exploration in progress). Nothing is implemented until this plan is approved.

## Context
(to fill)

## Ground rules for every milestone

1. **The guarantee** (spec §11): each job accepts at most one result; every succeeded job has
   exactly one accepted result; a job may execute more than once. It is enforced only by the
   token-guarded UPDATEs in `src/etf_risk/jobs/store.py` and checked by the existing
   `INVARIANT_QUERIES` / `JobStore.invariant_violations()` (store.py:127, :481). Rules for all
   milestones: nothing but `JobStore.accept_result` may produce an accepted attempt; cleanup never
   touches an accepted attempt's folder; the cache reads accepted runs only and never writes the
   job table; `invariant_violations()` must be empty after every test scenario and every
   experiment batch.
2. **Authorship** (spec §11, "Stages and authorship"): Claude Code writes the Compose services,
   the worker's pipeline integration, the CLIs, the fault-injection and measurement tooling and
   their tests; the project author writes the cache logic and the experiments (design,
   predictions, formal sessions, answers) with tutoring. For the author's parts Claude prepares
   scaffolds (signatures, docstrings, TODO markers, failing tests) and reviews, but does not fill
   them in. New files carry an `AI contribution:` line; experiment documents carry an authorship
   line as in `docs/partition-experiment.md`.
3. **Review gates**: every milestone starts with a findings report (no fixes before the author has
   seen it) and ends with a stop for review before its PR is merged.
4. **Git**: one branch and one PR per milestone, each in its own worktree from up-to-date `main`
   (`.claude/worktrees/<name>`), so the main worktree's uncommitted hook work never enters a
   milestone branch. Stage by explicit path; no AI logs in milestone commits (workstream W3);
   merge commits only; formal measurement sessions run on a merged, clean commit whose SHA goes
   into every run record. `gh` is not installed here: Claude pushes the branch, the author opens
   and merges the PR on GitHub.
5. **Privacy**: `data/` and the private plan stay out of Git; never print memory files,
   `.git/info/exclude` or app lists in tool calls.
6. **Measurement sessions**: while one runs, other sessions only write and review; wait for the
   explicit confirmation that it ended, then check that its worktree is unchanged.
7. **Wording**: explicit counts, no claims beyond what was measured, "one process" (never "one
   core"), and a "not claimed" list for each experiment.

## Cross-cutting requirements

**A. Code provenance for the jobs subpackage.** `provenance.code_state()` hashes only
`PACKAGE_DIR.glob("*.py")` (provenance.py:62), so nothing under `src/etf_risk/jobs/` (Python or
`schema/*.sql`) is identified by any record, and a naive recursive glob would collide on
`__init__.py`. Fix in M0: hash every `*.py` and `*.sql` under `src/etf_risk/` recursively, keyed by
package-relative POSIX path (`model.py` keeps its key; new keys such as `jobs/store.py`,
`jobs/schema/mysql.sql`), so older records stay comparable for the modules they cover. The
git clean flag already covers `src/`. From M1 on, every attempt folder gets an `attempt.json`
with the worker's `code_state()`, and every experiment record carries it. Authorship
provenance stays in each module's `AI contribution:` line.

**B. Reproducible dependencies.** `pymysql[rsa]==1.1.1` and `confluent-kafka==2.16.0` are
installed ad hoc with `uv run --with` (compose.yaml:13) and are not in `uv.lock`. M0 adds a
`jobs` dependency group with these exact pins; M3 adds a `cache` group with an exact `redis`
pin. Each `uv lock` change must only add packages: numpy 2.5.4, pandas 2.3.3, pyspark 4.2.0,
pyarrow 26.0.0 and psutil 7.2.2 unchanged, checked by diffing the lock. Every documented command
uses `uv run --group …` (never `--with`) and `uv sync --frozen`. Service images stay pinned by
digest (Redis added the same way). Host tools are recorded with each formal session (observed
2026-10-23: uv 0.11.16, Java 17.0.10, Docker 28.3.0, Compose v2.38.1, Docker Desktop VM 3.83 GiB).
The NumPy pin listed as planned in spec §9 stays out of scope unless approved.

**C. Startup commands.** One runbook (README section, linked from spec §11) gives the exact,
copy-pasteable commands per configuration: test services; the E1/E2 stack (MySQL, Kafka, native
worker, reconciler, submit, status); the E3 stack (Redis, query CLI, warm query service);
teardown with `down -v`. Each milestone's acceptance includes running its runbook commands as
written on a fresh worktree.

**D. Measured memory budgets.** A budget ledger in spec §11: component, limit, measured peak,
method, date, commit. Known: MySQL 512 MiB (peaks 324–511 MiB), Kafka 640 MiB (354–516 MiB),
pipeline container 2.5 GiB (stride 21: 2,282 / 2,342 MiB); native stride-21 pipeline peak summed
RSS 1.27 GiB median, with only 1.3–1.6 GiB free before those runs (spec §8). To measure: the
native worker with its pipeline tree (M1), reconciler and submit (M1), Redis 128 MiB with
`maxmemory` 32 MiB (M3), the warm query service (M3/M4), and the total per configuration against
the 3.83 GiB VM and the 8 GiB host. Container peaks come from cgroup `memory.peak` through a new
helper (today only `docker/run.sh` reads it, inside the pipeline container); native peaks from
`measure.py`'s sampler. Each recovery batch starts on a fresh MySQL container and records its own
peak (spec §11). A budget that is exceeded stops the session; budgets change only at review.

## Milestones (numbered as in the outline)

### M1 — Read the whole project and bring the code up to date
Branch `chore/extension-baseline` · Author: Claude Code · Prerequisite: the author merges
`fix/measure-process-kinds` (97c35f3, pushed, not yet in `main`), because M2–M5 sample memory
with `measure.py`'s process kinds.

1. **Audit, read-only.** A findings report for the author, nothing fixed yet. Already found:
   - provenance does not cover `jobs/` (cross-cutting A);
   - the jobs dependencies are not locked (cross-cutting B);
   - the merged worktrees `.claude/worktrees/job-queue` and `job-table` are clean and their
     branches are in `main`: remove them, with the author's OK;
   - (to fill from the exploration: CLIs, stale status text, test gaps)
2. **Fixes, after approval:** recursive provenance with package-relative keys; the `jobs`
   dependency group and lock; `--with` replaced by `--group jobs` everywhere; a container
   memory-peak helper; stale status text; the runbook skeleton (cross-cutting C).
3. **Revalidation:** offline suite; live job suite against fresh MySQL 8.4.13 and Kafka 4.3.1
   with `--group jobs`; MySQL and Kafka peaks read with the new helper.

Deliverables: findings report; code and doc changes above. Acceptance: a test enumerates every
`*.py`/`*.sql` under `src/etf_risk/` and finds each in `source_sha256` with a unique key, and the
top-level keys are unchanged; `uv lock --check` passes and the lock diff only adds the `jobs`
group's packages; live suite passes with the same case count as on e2806bd (379) or the
difference is explained; peaks within budget; no file outside the listed scope changed.
Tests: `tests/test_provenance.py` (new cases), job suites on SQLite and live.

(to fill: M2–M6)

## Separate workstreams (outside M0–M5)

No milestone branch touches these files, and no milestone waits on them.

- **W1 Data verification** (own branch, e.g. `data/verification`, own plan): the second-source
  comparison and terms-of-use review planned in spec §9, and the unverified extreme days (§10).
  The extension's experiments use the existing snapshot unchanged and claim nothing about the
  analysis results.
- **W2 Privacy-hook fixes** (own branch, e.g. `fix/transcript-privacy`): the uncommitted edits in
  the main worktree to `.claude/hooks/transcript_privacy.py`, `tests/test_transcript_privacy.py`
  and the transcript under `docs/ai-usage/2026-10-19_1643_c82fe879-23/`, plus the open hook items
  of spec §10 (separator rule, save timing, folders for interruption notices). Claude changes the
  hook only when asked to.
- **W3 AI-log review** (own branch or branches, e.g. `docs/ai-logs-<date>`): the untracked
  session folders under `docs/ai-usage/` and those each milestone produces, reviewed by the author
  and committed in separate "Add reviewed AI logs for …" commits, never together with code.
  Reviewing a milestone's logs can follow that milestone's merge.

## Verification

### M2 — The worker runs the real pipeline: heartbeats, fencing, timeouts, cleanup
Branch `feature/worker-pipeline` · Author: Claude Code (spec §11) · Depends on M1.

Design (all new code in `src/etf_risk/jobs/`; the store's SQL and guards stay as they are):
- **Job parameters.** A validated parameter set replaces free-form `params`: snapshot, window
  kind, window days, stride, anchor, sample ticker (draft; fixed after the pipeline report).
  `submit` computes `input_checksums` from the snapshot's return files and quality report, the
  same files `windows.py` records in `config.json`. The worker checks them before step 1; a
  mismatch fails the attempt as not retryable.
- **`pipeline.py`, `SubprocessPipeline`** (implements `worker.Pipeline`). Runs the three CLIs
  in order, each as `sys.executable -m …` with every output inside the attempt folder:
  `windows --out-root <run_dir>/windows`, `spark_pipeline --windows … --out-root
  <run_dir>/output --run-id <run id>`, `verify --run …`. Each step's working directory, `TMPDIR`
  and `SPARK_LOCAL_DIRS` point to `<run_dir>/.work`, so nothing lands in the shared `data/`
  folders or `/tmp`; stdout and stderr go to `<run_dir>/logs/<step>.log`. The run counts as a
  result only if every step exits 0, `checks.json` reports every check passed, `verify.json`
  reports no mismatch, and `run.json` exists. Then `.work` is removed and the worker accepts.
- **Heartbeats.** The worker thread waits on the child with `wait(timeout=…)` and calls
  `heartbeat()` every `lease / 4` (15 s with the 60 s default). There is no background thread, so
  the DB connection is used from one thread only. If a renewal raises (database unreachable),
  the worker retries at the next tick. Once the time since its last successful renewal
  reaches the lease minus a margin, it fences itself: it kills the run and raises `Fenced`.
  It assumes the lease is lost rather than risk two Spark runs on one machine.
- **Fencing.** `heartbeat()` false → terminate the step's process group (SIGTERM, grace,
  SIGKILL), raise `Fenced`; the folder stays and is never referenced. Token guards are unchanged.
- **Timeouts.** A wall-clock limit per step and per attempt, set from measured durations with a
  wide margin. Exceeding it kills the process group → `PipelineError(retryable=True)`, so the
  job is retried until `max_attempts`. Kafka `max.poll.interval.ms` and `session.timeout.ms` are
  set explicitly in `kafka.py`, with the poll interval above the attempt limit, and pinned by a test.
- **Cleanup.**
  - Children start in their own process group, behind a small launcher with a "lifeline"
    pipe: if the worker dies, even by SIGKILL, the launcher sees EOF and kills its group. This
    is needed because macOS has no parent-death signal.
  - At startup, a worker kills the process groups recorded in `.work/pgid` of unfinished
    attempts left by an earlier worker on the same output root.
  - `jobs cleanup` lists, and with `--delete` removes, the folders of attempts whose outcome is
    failed or expired and that ended longer than a grace period ago. Folders with no attempt row
    are reported but never deleted, and neither are accepted or running attempts. Dry run by default.
- **Graceful stop.** SIGTERM/SIGINT ends polling, kills a running step, and calls
  `fail_attempt(retryable=True)`, so the job is requeued at once instead of after its lease.
- **Event log.** Each process (worker, reconciler, submit) appends JSON lines with UTC times,
  one flushed line per event: delivered, claimed, renewed, renewal failed, step started or
  ended, fenced, accepted, failed, requeued, published. E2's times come from these logs and the
  tables. No new table is needed, and the store's transactions are unchanged.
- **CLI** `python -m etf_risk.jobs <command>`:
  - `init-db`: schema;
  - `create-topic`: wraps `kafka.create_topic`;
  - `submit`, `worker`, `reconciler`, `cleanup`;
  - `status [--check]`: prints the job and attempt tables and `invariant_violations()`, and
    exits 1 on any violation.

  Settings come from flags or `ETF_RISK_MYSQL_URL` / `ETF_RISK_KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP`, and logging is
  configured.
- **Defense in depth for the guarantee** (optional, small): a unique index on accepted attempts
  per job. SQLite: a partial unique index. MySQL: a unique index on a generated column that is
  `job_id` only when `outcome = 'accepted'`. A test shows that a second accepted row is refused.
- **Attempt record.** `<run_dir>/attempt.json` holds the worker id, run id, steps with exit
  codes and times, input checksums as checked, and `code_state()` (now covering `jobs/`).

  `windows --out-root <run_dir>/windows`, `spark_pipeline --windows … --out-root
  <run_dir>/output --run-id <run id>`, `verify --run …`. Each step's working directory, `TMPDIR`
  and `SPARK_LOCAL_DIRS` point to `<run_dir>/.work`, so nothing lands in the shared `data/`
  folders or `/tmp`; stdout and stderr go to `<run_dir>/logs/<step>.log`. The run counts as a
  result only if every step exits 0, `checks.json` reports every check passed, `verify.json`
  reports no mismatch, and `run.json` exists. Then `.work` is removed and the worker accepts.
- **Heartbeats.** The worker thread waits on the child with `wait(timeout=…)` and calls
  `heartbeat()` every `lease / 4` (15 s with the 60 s default). There is no background thread, so
  the DB connection is used from one thread only. If a renewal raises (database unreachable),
  the worker retries at the next tick. Once the time since its last successful renewal
  reaches the lease minus a margin, it fences itself: it kills the run and raises `Fenced`.
  It assumes the lease is lost rather than risk two Spark runs on one machine.
- **Fencing.** `heartbeat()` false → terminate the step's process group (SIGTERM, grace,
  SIGKILL), raise `Fenced`; the folder stays and is never referenced. Token guards are unchanged.
- **Timeouts.** A wall-clock limit per step and per attempt, set from measured durations with a
  wide margin. Exceeding it kills the process group → `PipelineError(retryable=True)`, so the
  job is retried until `max_attempts`. Kafka `max.poll.interval.ms` and `session.timeout.ms` are
  set explicitly in `kafka.py`, with the poll interval above the attempt limit, and pinned by a test.
- **Cleanup.**
  - Children start in their own process group, behind a small launcher with a "lifeline"
    pipe: if the worker dies, even by SIGKILL, the launcher sees EOF and kills its group. This
    is needed because macOS has no parent-death signal.
  - At startup, a worker kills the process groups recorded in `.work/pgid` of unfinished
    attempts left by an earlier worker on the same output root.
  - `jobs cleanup` lists, and with `--delete` removes, the folders of attempts whose outcome is
    failed or expired and that ended longer than a grace period ago. Folders with no attempt row
    are reported but never deleted, and neither are accepted or running attempts. Dry run by default.
- **Graceful stop.** SIGTERM/SIGINT ends polling, kills a running step, and calls
  `fail_attempt(retryable=True)`, so the job is requeued at once instead of after its lease.
- **Event log.** Each process (worker, reconciler, submit) appends JSON lines with UTC times,
  one flushed line per event: delivered, claimed, renewed, renewal failed, step started or
  ended, fenced, accepted, failed, requeued, published. E2's times come from these logs and the
  tables. No new table is needed, and the store's transactions are unchanged.
- **CLI** `python -m etf_risk.jobs <command>`:
  - `init-db`: schema;
  - `create-topic`: wraps `kafka.create_topic`;
  - `submit`, `worker`, `reconciler`, `cleanup`;
  - `status [--check]`: prints the job and attempt tables and `invariant_violations()`, and
    exits 1 on any violation.

  Settings come from flags or `ETF_RISK_MYSQL_URL` / `ETF_RISK_KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP`, and logging is
  configured.
- **Defense in depth for the guarantee** (optional, small): a unique index on accepted attempts
  per job. SQLite: a partial unique index. MySQL: a unique index on a generated column that is
  `job_id` only when `outcome = 'accepted'`. A test shows that a second accepted row is refused.
- **Attempt record.** `<run_dir>/attempt.json` holds the worker id, run id, steps with exit
  codes and times, input checksums as checked, and `code_state()` (now covering `jobs/`).

# Plan: finishing the systems extension (spec §11) in reviewed milestones

Status: DRAFT (exploration in progress). Nothing is implemented until this plan is approved.

## Context
(to fill)

## Ground rules for every milestone

1. **The guarantee** (spec §11): each job accepts at most one result; every succeeded job has
   exactly one accepted result; a job may execute more than once. It is enforced only by the
   token-guarded UPDATEs in `src/etf_risk/jobs/store.py` and checked by the existing
   `INVARIANT_QUERIES` / `JobStore.invariant_violations()` (store.py:127, :481). Rules for all
   milestones: nothing but `JobStore.accept_result` may produce an accepted attempt; cleanup never
   touches an accepted attempt's folder; the cache reads accepted runs only and never writes the
   job table; `invariant_violations()` must be empty after every test scenario and every
   experiment batch.
2. **Authorship** (spec §11, "Stages and authorship"): Claude Code writes the Compose services,
   the worker's pipeline integration, the CLIs, the fault-injection and measurement tooling and
   their tests; the project author writes the cache logic and the experiments (design,
   predictions, formal sessions, answers) with tutoring. For the author's parts Claude prepares
   scaffolds (signatures, docstrings, TODO markers, failing tests) and reviews, but does not fill
   them in. New files carry an `AI contribution:` line; experiment documents carry an authorship
   line as in `docs/partition-experiment.md`.
3. **Review gates**: every milestone starts with a findings report (no fixes before the author has
   seen it) and ends with a stop for review before its PR is merged.
4. **Git**: one branch and one PR per milestone, each in its own worktree from up-to-date `main`
   (`.claude/worktrees/<name>`), so the main worktree's uncommitted hook work never enters a
   milestone branch. Stage by explicit path; no AI logs in milestone commits (workstream W3);
   merge commits only; formal measurement sessions run on a merged, clean commit whose SHA goes
   into every run record. `gh` is not installed here: Claude pushes the branch, the author opens
   and merges the PR on GitHub.
5. **Privacy**: `data/` and the private plan stay out of Git; never print memory files,
   `.git/info/exclude` or app lists in tool calls.
6. **Measurement sessions**: while one runs, other sessions only write and review; wait for the
   explicit confirmation that it ended, then check that its worktree is unchanged.
7. **Wording**: explicit counts, no claims beyond what was measured, "one process" (never "one
   core"), and a "not claimed" list for each experiment.

## Cross-cutting requirements

**A. Code provenance for the jobs subpackage.** `provenance.code_state()` hashes only
`PACKAGE_DIR.glob("*.py")` (provenance.py:62), so nothing under `src/etf_risk/jobs/` (Python or
`schema/*.sql`) is identified by any record, and a naive recursive glob would collide on
`__init__.py`. Fix in M0: hash every `*.py` and `*.sql` under `src/etf_risk/` recursively, keyed by
package-relative POSIX path (`model.py` keeps its key; new keys such as `jobs/store.py`,
`jobs/schema/mysql.sql`), so older records stay comparable for the modules they cover. The
git clean flag already covers `src/`. From M1 on, every attempt folder gets an `attempt.json`
with the worker's `code_state()`, and every experiment record carries it. Authorship
provenance stays in each module's `AI contribution:` line.

**B. Reproducible dependencies.** `pymysql[rsa]==1.1.1` and `confluent-kafka==2.16.0` are
installed ad hoc with `uv run --with` (compose.yaml:13) and are not in `uv.lock`. M0 adds a
`jobs` dependency group with these exact pins; M3 adds a `cache` group with an exact `redis`
pin. Each `uv lock` change must only add packages: numpy 2.5.4, pandas 2.3.3, pyspark 4.2.0,
pyarrow 26.0.0 and psutil 7.2.2 unchanged, checked by diffing the lock. Every documented command
uses `uv run --group …` (never `--with`) and `uv sync --frozen`. Service images stay pinned by
digest (Redis added the same way). Host tools are recorded with each formal session (observed
2026-10-23: uv 0.11.16, Java 17.0.10, Docker 28.3.0, Compose v2.38.1, Docker Desktop VM 3.83 GiB).
The NumPy pin listed as planned in spec §9 stays out of scope unless approved.

**C. Startup commands.** One runbook (README section, linked from spec §11) gives the exact,
copy-pasteable commands per configuration: test services; the E1/E2 stack (MySQL, Kafka, native
worker, reconciler, submit, status); the E3 stack (Redis, query CLI, warm query service);
teardown with `down -v`. Each milestone's acceptance includes running its runbook commands as
written on a fresh worktree.

**D. Measured memory budgets.** A budget ledger in spec §11: component, limit, measured peak,
method, date, commit. Known: MySQL 512 MiB (peaks 324–511 MiB), Kafka 640 MiB (354–516 MiB),
pipeline container 2.5 GiB (stride 21: 2,282 / 2,342 MiB); native stride-21 pipeline peak summed
RSS 1.27 GiB median, with only 1.3–1.6 GiB free before those runs (spec §8). To measure: the
native worker with its pipeline tree (M1), reconciler and submit (M1), Redis 128 MiB with
`maxmemory` 32 MiB (M3), the warm query service (M3/M4), and the total per configuration against
the 3.83 GiB VM and the 8 GiB host. Container peaks come from cgroup `memory.peak` through a new
helper (today only `docker/run.sh` reads it, inside the pipeline container); native peaks from
`measure.py`'s sampler. Each recovery batch starts on a fresh MySQL container and records its own
peak (spec §11). A budget that is exceeded stops the session; budgets change only at review.

### M1 — Read the whole project and bring the code up to date
Branch `chore/extension-baseline` · Author: Claude Code · Prerequisite: the author merges
`fix/measure-process-kinds` (97c35f3, pushed, not yet in `main`), because M2–M5 sample memory
with `measure.py`'s process kinds.

1. **Audit, read-only.** A findings report for the author, nothing fixed yet. Already found:
   - provenance does not cover `jobs/` (cross-cutting A);
   - the jobs dependencies are not locked (cross-cutting B);
   - the merged worktrees `.claude/worktrees/job-queue` and `job-table` are clean and their
     branches are in `main`: remove them, with the author's OK;
   - the jobs package has no entry point (no `__main__`, argparse or `[project.scripts]`):
     the "submit CLI" of the spec §11 diagram does not exist, and nothing configures logging
     (the reconciler's per-pass INFO line is never shown);
   - nothing is timed: `Pass` and `Served` hold counts only; no `requeued_at` or status
     history; `published_at` is cleared by the claim; a crash before the claim leaves no trace;
   - Kafka's `session.timeout.ms` and `max.poll.interval.ms` are library defaults (45 s, 300 s),
     unpinned by any test, while `serve()` runs the pipeline inside its poll loop;
   - the 22 mutation checks of the job docs exist only as prose (no script, not reproducible);
   - doc drift: `job-table.md` claim SQL omits `published_at = NULL` (store.py:334) and
     "apart from submit" omits `mark_published`; `job-queue.md:90` names a test that does not
     exercise the lost confirmation of the job-9 timeline;
   - the test helper `WorkerEnv.check` (tests/jobs_backends.py:200) ties result checks to the
     simulated pipeline's `result.json`;
   - (to fill from the remaining exploration: pipeline CLIs, stale status text)
2. **Fixes, after approval:** recursive provenance with package-relative keys; the `jobs`
   dependency group and lock; `--with` replaced by `--group jobs` everywhere; a container
   memory-peak helper; stale status text; the runbook skeleton (cross-cutting C).
3. **Revalidation:** offline suite; live job suite against fresh MySQL 8.4.13 and Kafka 4.3.1
   with `--group jobs`; MySQL and Kafka peaks read with the new helper.

Deliverables: findings report; code and doc changes above. Acceptance: a test enumerates every
`*.py`/`*.sql` under `src/etf_risk/` and finds each in `source_sha256` with a unique key, and the
top-level keys are unchanged; `uv lock --check` passes and the lock diff only adds the `jobs`
group's packages; live suite passes with the same case count as on e2806bd (379) or the
difference is explained; peaks within budget; no file outside the listed scope changed.
Tests: `tests/test_provenance.py` (new cases), job suites on SQLite and live.

(to fill: M2–M6)

## Separate workstreams (outside M0–M5)

No milestone branch touches these files, and no milestone waits on them.

- **W1 Data verification** (own branch, e.g. `data/verification`, own plan): the second-source
  comparison and terms-of-use review planned in spec §9, and the unverified extreme days (§10).
  The extension's experiments use the existing snapshot unchanged and claim nothing about the

- **W2 Privacy-hook fixes** (own branch, e.g. `fix/transcript-privacy`): the uncommitted edits in

- **W3 AI-log review** (own branch or branches, e.g. `docs/ai-logs-<date>`): the untracked

  Reviewing a milestone's logs can follow that milestone's merge.

## 1. The CLIs

**`etf_risk.windows`** (argparse at `windows.py:330-341`)
- **Arguments:**
  - `--snapshot` (required), `--kind {rolling, calendar-year, full-period}` (required).
  - `--processed-root` (default `data/processed`), `--out-root` (default `data/windows`).
  - `--window-days` 252, `--stride` 21, `--anchor` `"1980-01-02"`.
  - `--allow-dense-stride`, `--name`, `--overwrite`.
  - A stride below 21 without `--allow-dense-stride` triggers `parser.error`, exit 2 (`343-344`).
- **No `--tickers` or `--leverages`.** The tickers are every `*.parquet` file in `<snapshot>/daily_returns/` (`92`). Tickers are chosen earlier, by `ingest --tickers` (`ingest.py:172`) or `download --tickers`.
- **Reads:** `daily_returns/*.parquet`, `quality_report.json` (`237-238`) and the NYSE calendar.
- **Writes:** `<out-root>/<snapshot>/<name>/` (`348`): first `windows.parquet`, then `config.json` (`300-302`).
- **Folder name:** `default_name()` gives `rolling-<days>-s<stride>`, or the kind name for the other kinds (`325-326`). It ignores `--anchor`. The caller picks the root and the name, but the snapshot folder is always inserted.
- **Overwrite rule:** it refuses only when `config.json` already exists: "already has window definitions (use --overwrite)" (`297-298`). An existing folder without `config.json` is accepted. `README.md:224` says it "refuses an existing folder", which is broader than the code.
- **Exit codes:** there are none of its own. It returns 0 (`355`). The self-check `ValueError` (`263-264`), `FileExistsError` and `FileNotFoundError` (`101`) propagate as Python's exit 1; argparse errors give 2.
- **Speed:** four window sets (strides 21, 14, 7, 3) were built in 5 s in total (`experiments.md:70-71`).

**`etf_risk.spark_pipeline`** (`build_parser`, `666-683`)
- **Arguments:**
  - `--windows` (required), `--out-root` (default `data/outputs/windows`).
  - `--run-id`: default is `"run-" + UTC %Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ` (`717`), one-second resolution, used as a path component without validation.
  - `--initial-nav` 100, `--master` `local[*]`.
  - `--shuffle-partitions`, `--coalesce on|off`, `--record-plans`, `--cache none|members|members-checks`.
- **Leverages are fixed:** `LEVERAGES = (1.0, 2.0)` (`83`), and `pair_paths` raises for anything else (`299-300`).
- **Reads:**
  - It first runs `verify_checksums(--windows)` (`718-722`).
  - Then it reads `windows.parquet` and the return files listed in the config, resolved against the repository root (`758-760`).
- **Run folder:** always `<out-root>/<config.snapshot>/<windows folder name>/<run-id>` (`run_dir_for`, `654-656`). It cannot be told to write into an exact folder.
  - If that folder exists it prints "exists; use a new --run-id" and returns 2 (`724-726`).
  - It runs `mkdir(parents=True)` before Spark starts (`727`).
  - `demo.md:60-61` confirms the pattern: `--out-root data/outputs-demo --run-id demo-1` writes to `data/outputs-demo/full-2026-10-12/calendar-year-r2/demo-1`.
- **Exit codes** (docstring `49`): 0 all checks passed, 1 a check failed, 2 the run failed, 3 checksum error (Spark never starts).
  - Exit 2 covers: an exception inside the `try` (`745-778`), an existing run folder, or the partition flags used inside an existing Spark session (`712-716`).

## Surprises and gaps

1. **Folder contract mismatch.** The worker pre-creates its folder. `spark_pipeline` builds its own nested path and refuses one that exists. `windows` only refuses if `config.json` exists.
2. **Exit code 1 is ambiguous.** It also means an uncaught exception in all three CLIs, so it can't be told apart from "checks failed" (pipeline) or "mismatch" (verify). A killed run leaves no `run.json` to check instead.
3. **`run.json` is only written at the end.** There is no on-disk "running" record.
4. **Working directory matters.** verify uses `run.json`'s `windows_dir` as stored (`verify.py:185`) but resolves `snapshot_dir` against the repository root (`191`). Relative paths therefore assume the commands run from the repository root.
5. **`windows --overwrite` rewrites files in place.** Runs refer to the windows folder by path, so a later verify of an older run would fail its checksum check with exit 3 (inferred).
6. **The 60 s default lease is shorter than some runs.** Native `spark_pipeline` takes 18–47 s at stride 21, plus about 14 s for verify; the Docker pipeline alone took 67 s.
7. **The SQL scripts can't be reused as-is.** They have no functions, only print, start their own session each time, and record no timings.

**Not checked:** Spark's internal `_temporary`/warehouse behavior, the exact SIGINT exit code, native verify memory and its timing on current code, contents of any file under `data/`, and `jobs/kafka.py`, `jobs/mysql.py` and `jobs/reconciler.py` beyond the constants cited.</result>

Since the pandas baseline, `position` writes these checks into the log at every start (pandas :128-130).

def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    started = time.perf_counter()
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    sets_spark = args.shuffle_partitions is not None or args.coalesce is not None
    if sets_spark and SparkSession.getActiveSession() is not None:
        print("--shuffle-partitions and --coalesce need a fresh process: a Spark session already exists here, "
              "and building one would change its settings", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    run_id = args.run_id or "run-" + datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ")
    try:
        config, verified = verify_checksums(args.windows)
    except (ChecksumError, FileNotFoundError, KeyError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
        print(f"checksum verification failed, Spark not started:\n{exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 3
    run_dir = run_dir_for(args.windows, args.out_root, run_id)
    if run_dir.exists():
        print(f"{run_dir} exists; use a new --run-id", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    run_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
    record = {
        "run_id": run_id, "started_at_utc": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "code": code_state(), "windows_dir": str(args.windows),
        "windows_config": config, "verified_sha256": verified, "leverages": list(LEVERAGES),
        "initial_nav": args.initial_nav, "environment": environment(), "status": "running",
    }
    if sets_spark or args.record_plans or args.cache is not None:     # without the flags, run.json is as before
        record["pipeline_options"] = {"shuffle_partitions": args.shuffle_partitions, "coalesce": args.coalesce,
                                      "record_plans": args.record_plans}
        if args.cache is not None:
            record["pipeline_options"]["cache"] = args.cache
    timings: dict[str, float] = {}
    status, code = "failed", 2
    spark = None
    caches = None
    own_session = SparkSession.getActiveSession() is None      # only stop a session started here
    plan_after, plan_start_error = None, None
    try:
        t = time.perf_counter()
        spark = build_spark(args.master, args.shuffle_partitions,
                            None if args.coalesce is None else args.coalesce == "on")
        timings["session_start"] = time.perf_counter() - t
        record["spark"] = spark_settings(spark)
        if args.record_plans:                    # the executions after this id are this run's
            t = time.perf_counter()
            try:
                plan_after = plans.watermark(spark)
            except Exception as exc:
                plan_start_error = "".join(traceback.format_exception_only(type(exc), exc)).strip()[-500:]
            timings["plan_capture"] = time.perf_counter() - t
        defs = spark.read.parquet(str(args.windows / config["windows_file"]))
        return_files = [str(resolve(config["snapshot_dir"]) / rel) for rel in config["inputs_sha256"] if rel.startswith("daily_returns/")]
        returns = spark.read.parquet(*return_files)

## Surprises and gaps

1. **Folder contract mismatch.** The worker pre-creates its folder. `spark_pipeline` builds its own nested path and refuses one that exists. `windows` only refuses if `config.json` exists.
2. **Exit code 1 is ambiguous.** It also means an uncaught exception in all three CLIs, so it can't be told apart from "checks failed" (pipeline) or "mismatch" (verify). A killed run leaves no `run.json` to check instead.
3. **`run.json` is only written at the end.** There is no on-disk "running" record.
4. **Working directory matters.** verify uses `run.json`'s `windows_dir` as stored (`verify.py:185`) but resolves `snapshot_dir` against the repository root (`191`). Relative paths therefore assume the commands run from the repository root.
5. **`windows --overwrite` rewrites files in place.** Runs refer to the windows folder by path, so a later verify of an older run would fail its checksum check with exit 3 (inferred).
6. **The 60 s default lease is shorter than some runs.** Native `spark_pipeline` takes 18–47 s at stride 21, plus about 14 s for verify; the Docker pipeline alone took 67 s.
7. **The SQL scripts can't be reused as-is.** They have no functions, only print, start their own session each time, and record no timings.

## 1. The CLIs

**`etf_risk.windows`** (argparse at `windows.py:330-341`)
- **Arguments:**

- **Writes:** `<out-root>/<snapshot>/<name>/` (`348`): first `windows.parquet`, then `config.json` (`300-302`).
- **Folder name:** `default_name()` gives `rolling-<days>-s<stride>`, or the kind name for the other kinds (`325-326`). It ignores `--anchor`. The caller picks the root and the name, but the snapshot folder is always inserted.
- **Overwrite rule:** it refuses only when `config.json` already exists: "already has window definitions (use --overwrite)" (`297-298`). An existing folder without `config.json` is accepted. `README.md:224` says it "refuses an existing folder", which is broader than the code.
- **Exit codes:** there are none of its own. It returns 0 (`355`). The self-check `ValueError` (`263-264`), `FileExistsError` and `FileNotFoundError` (`101`) propagate as Python's exit 1; argparse errors give 2.
- **Speed:** four window sets (strides 21, 14, 7, 3) were built in 5 s in total (`experiments.md:70-71`).

**`etf_risk.spark_pipeline`** (`build_parser`, `666-683`)
- **Arguments:**
  - `--windows` (required), `--out-root` (default `data/outputs/windows`).
  - `--run-id`: default is `"run-" + UTC %Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ` (`717`), one-second resolution, used as a path component without validation.
  - `--initial-nav` 100, `--master` `local[*]`.
  - `--shuffle-partitions`, `--coalesce on|off`, `--record-plans`, `--cache none|members|members-checks`.

- **Exit codes** (docstring `49`): 0 all checks passed, 1 a check failed, 2 the run failed, 3 checksum error (Spark never starts).

  - No long-lived session server exists.
  - Inferred gap: `stage_task_counts` reads every job of a job group (`598-606`), so in a reused session it would count earlier runs too. `plans.watermark` was designed for that case (`plans.py:86-91`).

1. **Folder contract mismatch.** The worker pre-creates its folder. `spark_pipeline` builds its own nested path and refuses one that exists. `windows` only refuses if `config.json` exists.
2. **Exit code 1 is ambiguous.** It also means an uncaught exception in all three CLIs, so it can't be told apart from "checks failed" (pipeline) or "mismatch" (verify). A killed run leaves no `run.json` to check instead.
3. **`run.json` is only written at the end.** There is no on-disk "running" record.
4. **Working directory matters.** verify uses `run.json`'s `windows_dir` as stored (`verify.py:185`) but resolves `snapshot_dir` against the repository root (`191`). Relative paths therefore assume the commands run from the repository root.
5. **`windows --overwrite` rewrites files in place.** Runs refer to the windows folder by path, so a later verify of an older run would fail its checksum check with exit 3 (inferred).
6. **The 60 s default lease is shorter than some runs.** Native `spark_pipeline` takes 18–47 s at stride 21, plus about 14 s for verify; the Docker pipeline alone took 67 s.
7. **The SQL scripts can't be reused as-is.** They have no functions, only print, start their own session each time, and record no timings.

## Surprises and gaps

1. **Folder contract mismatch.** The worker pre-creates its folder. `spark_pipeline` builds its own nested path and refuses one that exists. `windows` only refuses if `config.json` exists.
2. **Exit code 1 is ambiguous.** It also means an uncaught exception in all three CLIs, so it can't be told apart from "checks failed" (pipeline) or "mismatch" (verify). A killed run leaves no `run.json` to check instead.
3. **`run.json` is only written at the end.** There is no on-disk "running" record.
4. **Working directory matters.** verify uses `run.json`'s `windows_dir` as stored (`verify.py:185`) but resolves `snapshot_dir` against the repository root (`191`). Relative paths therefore assume the commands run from the repository root.
5. **`windows --overwrite` rewrites files in place.** Runs refer to the windows folder by path, so a later verify of an older run would fail its checksum check with exit 3 (inferred).
6. **The 60 s default lease is shorter than some runs.** Native `spark_pipeline` takes 18–47 s at stride 21, plus about 14 s for verify; the Docker pipeline alone took 67 s.
7. **The SQL scripts can't be reused as-is.** They have no functions, only print, start their own session each time, and record no timings.

  - `--allow-dense-stride`, `--name`, `--overwrite`.

**Non-atomic writes:**
- Every JSON file uses `Path.write_text`, which truncates and then writes. There are no temp-then-rename writes.

- **Exception inside the `try`:** `run.json` is written with status `failed` and an `error` field (`777-788`).
- **SIGINT:** `except Exception` does not catch it but the `finally` runs, which would give status `failed` with no `error` field. This is inferred from the code; not checked.
- **Construction-check failure:** an early return (`573-574`) leaves only `window_stats/`, plus `checks.json` and `run.json` with status `checks_failed`, exit 1.
- **Completeness marker:** the project treats a table as complete only if it has `_SUCCESS` (`caching-experiment.md:276-280`; `output_state` in `collect_caching_measurements.py:96-101`). `plots.py:82-86` and `167-188` require `paired/_SUCCESS`, `path_days/_SUCCESS` and status ok.

## Surprises and gaps

1. **Folder contract mismatch.** The worker pre-creates its folder. `spark_pipeline` builds its own nested path and refuses one that exists. `windows` only refuses if `config.json` exists.
2. **Exit code 1 is ambiguous.** It also means an uncaught exception in all three CLIs, so it can't be told apart from "checks failed" (pipeline) or "mismatch" (verify). A killed run leaves no `run.json` to check instead.
3. **`run.json` is only written at the end.** There is no on-disk "running" record.
4. **Working directory matters.** verify uses `run.json`'s `windows_dir` as stored (`verify.py:185`) but resolves `snapshot_dir` against the repository root (`191`). Relative paths therefore assume the commands run from the repository root.
5. **`windows --overwrite` rewrites files in place.** Runs refer to the windows folder by path, so a later verify of an older run would fail its checksum check with exit 3 (inferred).
6. **The 60 s default lease is shorter than some runs.** Native `spark_pipeline` takes 18–47 s at stride 21, plus about 14 s for verify; the Docker pipeline alone took 67 s.
7. **The SQL scripts can't be reused as-is.** They have no functions, only print, start their own session each time, and record no timings.

**Not checked:** Spark's internal `_temporary`/warehouse behavior, the exact SIGINT exit code, native verify memory and its timing on current code, contents of any file under `data/`, and `jobs/kafka.py`, `jobs/mysql.py` and `jobs/reconciler.py` beyond the constants cited.</result>

## 1. The CLIs

**`etf_risk.windows`** (argparse at `windows.py:330-341`)
- **Arguments:**
  - `--snapshot` (required), `--kind {rolling, calendar-year, full-period}` (required).
  - `--processed-root` (default `data/processed`), `--out-root` (default `data/windows`).
  - `--window-days` 252, `--stride` 21, `--anchor` `"1980-01-02"`.
  - `--allow-dense-stride`, `--name`, `--overwrite`.
  - A stride below 21 without `--allow-dense-stride` triggers `parser.error`, exit 2 (`343-344`).
- **No `--tickers` or `--leverages`.** The tickers are every `*.parquet` file in `<snapshot>/daily_returns/` (`92`). Tickers are chosen earlier, by `ingest --tickers` (`ingest.py:172`) or `download --tickers`.
- **Reads:** `daily_returns/*.parquet`, `quality_report.json` (`237-238`) and the NYSE calendar.
- **Writes:** `<out-root>/<snapshot>/<name>/` (`348`): first `windows.parquet`, then `config.json` (`300-302`).
- **Folder name:** `default_name()` gives `rolling-<days>-s<stride>`, or the kind name for the other kinds (`325-326`). It ignores `--anchor`. The caller picks the root and the name, but the snapshot folder is always inserted.
- **Overwrite rule:** it refuses only when `config.json` already exists: "already has window definitions (use --overwrite)" (`297-298`). An existing folder without `config.json` is accepted. `README.md:224` says it "refuses an existing folder", which is broader than the code.
- **Exit codes:** there are none of its own. It returns 0 (`355`). The self-check `ValueError` (`263-264`), `FileExistsError` and `FileNotFoundError` (`101`) propagate as Python's exit 1; argparse errors give 2.
- **Speed:** four window sets (strides 21, 14, 7, 3) were built in 5 s in total (`experiments.md:70-71`).

**`etf_risk.spark_pipeline`** (`build_parser`, `666-683`)
- **Arguments:**
  - `--windows` (required), `--out-root` (default `data/outputs/windows`).
  - `--run-id`: default is `"run-" + UTC %Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ` (`717`), one-second resolution, used as a path component without validation.
  - `--initial-nav` 100, `--master` `local[*]`.
  - `--shuffle-partitions`, `--coalesce on|off`, `--record-plans`, `--cache none|members|members-checks`.
- **Leverages are fixed:** `LEVERAGES = (1.0, 2.0)` (`83`), and `pair_paths` raises for anything else (`299-300`).
- **Reads:**
  - It first runs `verify_checksums(--windows)` (`718-722`).
  - Then it reads `windows.parquet` and the return files listed in the config, resolved against the repository root (`758-760`).
- **Run folder:** always `<out-root>/<config.snapshot>/<windows folder name>/<run-id>` (`run_dir_for`, `654-656`). It cannot be told to write into an exact folder.
  - If that folder exists it prints "exists; use a new --run-id" and returns 2 (`724-726`).
  - It runs `mkdir(parents=True)` before Spark starts (`727`).
  - `demo.md:60-61` confirms the pattern: `--out-root data/outputs-demo --run-id demo-1` writes to `data/outputs-demo/full-2026-10-12/calendar-year-r2/demo-1`.
- **Exit codes** (docstring `49`): 0 all checks passed, 1 a check failed, 2 the run failed, 3 checksum error (Spark never starts).
  - Exit 2 covers: an exception inside the `try` (`745-778`), an existing run folder, or the partition flags used inside an existing Spark session (`712-716`).
- **Gap:** exceptions outside the `try` exit with Python's default 1, which is the same code as "checks failed". This covers `mkdir` at `727`, building the record at `728-733`, and writing `run.json` in the `finally` at `788`.
- **Spec §4:** run output is `data/outputs/windows/<snapshot>/<name>/<run id>/` (`spec.md:128`); window definitions are `data/windows/<snapshot>/<name>/` (`spec.md:127`).
- **Other run-id schemes:** `measure` uses `run-<stamp>-<i>` (`measure.py:174`); the job store uses `job-<id>-attempt-<n>` (`store.py:231-233`).

**`etf_risk.verify`** (`178-181`)
- **Arguments:** `--run` (required; the exact run folder), `--sample-ticker` (default AAPL).
- **Reads:**
  - `<run>/run.json` (`184`), taking `windows_dir` from it as stored (`185`), then `verify_checksums` (`186-190`).
  - The returns, via `resolve(snapshot_dir)` (`191`).
  - `paired/` and `path_summary/` through Spark (`201`, `206`).
- **Writes:** `<run>/verify.json` (`221`), silently overwriting an existing one.
- **Exit codes:** 0 clean, 1 mismatch (`228`), 3 checksum error.
  - The checksum handler catches `ChecksumError`, `FileNotFoundError` and `KeyError`, but not `JSONDecodeError`, unlike the pipeline at `spark_pipeline.py:720`.

- It does not check the run's status before comparing.
- `spark.stop()` runs only on the success path (`222-223`), not in a `finally`.

**`etf_risk.measure`**: `[--repeats 4] [--interval 0.25] [--threshold-fraction 0.60] [--pipeline spark|pandas] -- <pipeline args>` (`227-240`). The `--` is mandatory (exit 2 otherwise, `229-232`); it exits 1 if the protocol stopped early (`269`). It needs `--group measure` for psutil (`pyproject.toml:19-21`).

**`plans.py`** has no CLI. It is used through `--record-plans` (`spark_pipeline.py:689-706`); on a capture failure it deletes `plans.json` (`703`) and the exit code is unchanged.

**`pandas_pipeline.py`** takes the same `--windows`, `--out-root`, `--run-id` and `--initial-nav` (`603-606`). It has the same `run_dir_for` (`596`), refuses an existing run folder (`620-622`), and uses the same exit codes.

**Who writes what:**

| Output | Written by | Where in code |
|---|---|---|
| `window_stats/`, `path_days/` (partitioned into `ticker=<T>/`), `path_summary/`, `paired/` | `compute()` → `materialize()`: `df.write.mode("error")…parquet()`, then read back | `spark_pipeline.py:553-560`, called at `566-588` |

| `verify.json` | verify | `verify.py:221` |
| `protocol-<stamp>.json`, `<run id>.log` | measure, next to the run folders | `measure.py:177`, `258` |

- The initial `"status": "running"` (`732`) is never written to disk.
- An observed stride-21 run folder (names only) holds those files and folders. Each table has `_SUCCESS`, `._SUCCESS.crc`, `part-*.snappy.parquet` and `.part-*.crc` files. There are no `_temporary` folders anywhere under `data/`, and every `run-*` folder has a `run.json`.

**Non-atomic writes:**
- Every JSON file uses `Path.write_text`, which truncates and then writes. There are no temp-then-rename writes.
- `windows.py` writes the Parquet file before `config.json`. A crash in between leaves an orphan `windows.parquet`, which the next run (without `--overwrite`) silently overwrites.
- **Killed with SIGTERM or SIGKILL:** the `finally` does not run, so there is no `run.json` (and possibly no `checks.json`) and tables are left partial. The docs say an aborted run "keeps whatever the pipeline had written (for example `window_stats/` and an incomplete `path_days/`)" (`experiments.md:319-321`); measure recorded exit −15 (`experiments.md:328`).
- **Exception inside the `try`:** `run.json` is written with status `failed` and an `error` field (`777-788`).
- **SIGINT:** `except Exception` does not catch it but the `finally` runs, which would give status `failed` with no `error` field. This is inferred from the code; not checked.
- **Construction-check failure:** an early return (`573-574`) leaves only `window_stats/`, plus `checks.json` and `run.json` with status `checks_failed`, exit 1.
- **Completeness marker:** the project treats a table as complete only if it has `_SUCCESS` (`caching-experiment.md:276-280`; `output_state` in `collect_caching_measurements.py:96-101`). `plots.py:82-86` and `167-188` require `paired/_SUCCESS`, `path_days/_SUCCESS` and status ok.
- Spark's internal `_temporary` commit mechanics: not checked in code.

**Scratch folders:**
- No `spark.local.dir`, warehouse, Hive or checkpoint settings or calls exist in `src/`.
- There is an empty, untracked `spark-warehouse/` at the repository root, created 2026-10-13 21:43, the evening the SQL analyses were committed (7278f0c). `.gitignore:224-227` ignores `spark-warehouse/`, `metastore_db/` and `derby.log`; the last two don't exist. It looks like Spark creates this folder in the working directory (inferred).
- The docs check for `spark-*` and `blockmgr-*` folders in `$TMPDIR` and `/private/tmp` after aborts (`experiments.md:315-317`; `caching-session.zsh:75-77`). One kill at 19 s left no folder, and the JVM exited within about 1 s, but the docs say this is "not guaranteed in every situation" (`experiments.md:324-339`).

## Surprises and gaps

1. **Folder contract mismatch.** The worker pre-creates its folder. `spark_pipeline` builds its own nested path and refuses one that exists. `windows` only refuses if `config.json` exists.
2. **Exit code 1 is ambiguous.** It also means an uncaught exception in all three CLIs, so it can't be told apart from "checks failed" (pipeline) or "mismatch" (verify). A killed run leaves no `run.json` to check instead.
3. **`run.json` is only written at the end.** There is no on-disk "running" record.
4. **Working directory matters.** verify uses `run.json`'s `windows_dir` as stored (`verify.py:185`) but resolves `snapshot_dir` against the repository root (`191`). Relative paths therefore assume the commands run from the repository root.
5. **`windows --overwrite` rewrites files in place.** Runs refer to the windows folder by path, so a later verify of an older run would fail its checksum check with exit 3 (inferred).
6. **The 60 s default lease is shorter than some runs.** Native `spark_pipeline` takes 18–47 s at stride 21, plus about 14 s for verify; the Docker pipeline alone took 67 s.
7. **The SQL scripts can't be reused as-is.** They have no functions, only print, start their own session each time, and record no timings.

**Not checked:** Spark's internal `_temporary`/warehouse behavior, the exact SIGINT exit code, native verify memory and its timing on current code, contents of any file under `data/`, and `jobs/kafka.py`, `jobs/mysql.py` and `jobs/reconciler.py` beyond the constants cited.</result>

## 2. Measurement tooling

**Collectors** (in `~/leveraged-etf-risk-analytics/analysis/`):
- **Stride, `collect_measurements.py`:**
  - Reads protocol JSONs and `run.json` files and writes `data/outputs-experiments/measurements.csv` (:24-26).
  - Stops unless there are 5 protocols with consistent runs, hashes and roles (`~/leveraged-etf-risk-analytics/docs/experiments.md:598-602`).
  - Roles come from a hard-coded `ROLES` map (:47-56). Fixed column order and line ending make a rebuild byte-identical (:196-208). It writes no `acceptance.json`.
- **Batch collectors** (partition, baseline, caching):
  - `--batch <folder>` reads `positions.tsv`, each configuration's `protocol-*.json`, `run.json`, `plans.json` and Parquet tables.
  - It writes `measurements.csv` and `acceptance.json` into the batch folder and exits 1 if any criterion fails (caching docstring :1-27, main :488-513).
  - `acceptance.json` holds batch, windows, repeats, reference_run, used_protocols, criteria (ok and problems), all_ok and notes (caching :453-461, partition :542-550, baseline :292-300).
  - `CRITERIA = ("1 code state", "2 inputs", "3 settings", "4 results", "5 completeness")` (partition :73).
  - `--check-protocol <JSON> --config A|B|C` (`--engine S|P` for the baseline) checks one protocol; the session helpers run it after each protocol.
  - Later collectors import the partition collector unchanged (caching :22-24, :42), and earlier scripts are never edited (`~/leveraged-etf-risk-analytics/docs/partition-experiment.md:310-311`).
  - A run with missing outputs is reported as a problem, not a crash (caching :18-20).

**Session helpers** (`~/leveraged-etf-risk-analytics/docs/caching-session.zsh`, the newest):
- Loaded with `source <repository>/docs/caching-session.zsh` in two Terminal windows. Loading only defines functions, sets variables and changes into the repository (:4-6, :17-18).
- Variables: `BATCH`, `CACHE_LOAD_MAX`, `CACHE_BOOT_MIN`, dry-run overrides, the order, and the abort limits `CACHE_ABORT_S=(A 80 B 80 C 81)` (:8-35).
- Functions:
  - `steps` (:38-73), `prechecks` (:85-98), `pause5` (:100-104), `ready` (:107-119).
  - `position n` refuses 1–6 violations and missing limits, then writes the checks, runs `measure`, runs `--check-protocol`, appends to `positions.tsv`, and prints STOP on failure (:125-150).
  - `where`, `watch_runs`, `abort_run`, `after_abort`, `note` (:152-222).
- How a session runs: window 2 runs `watch_runs`; window 1 runs `pause5 && ready && position n`, then `note 'position n: 4 ok, nothing unusual'`. Any stop means "come back to Claude", and "No git commits during the session" (:47-69).
- The stride helper is older: it is sourced from `~`, hard-codes the repository path, and uses `avail` and `protocol` (`~/leveraged-etf-risk-analytics/docs/stride-session.zsh:3`, :7, :71, :81).
- Each experiment adds a new helper file. Old ones stay unchanged because documents cite them by hash (partition :315-316).

**`~/leveraged-etf-risk-analytics/docs/measurements/README.md`** (main):
- Holds committed, reviewed copies, in a table: File | Experiment | Copy of | Rows | Columns (:12-17). "Each row is a started run, warm-ups included" (:19-20).
- Gives the check and rebuild commands (:22-36).
- "Updating a copy … is a reviewed change: copy the collector's output over the file here, then update the experiment document, `DOCUMENTED` in `src/etf_risk/plots.py` and the figures" (:44-46).

**CSV column conventions:**
- "Names carry their units: _s seconds, _bytes bytes" (`collect_measurements.py:31`).
- Values are unrounded, with booleans as True/False (experiments.md:604-605); `wall_excl_capture_s` is rounded to milliseconds (partition :839).
- Identity columns come first: batch, position, config/engine, used, protocol_id, run_id, … (`collect_caching_measurements.py:78-85`). Per-table comparison results are in `<table>_vs_reference` columns.
- `positions.tsv` columns: position, config, protocol, measure_exit, \<check\>, logged_at_utc (`collect_partition_measurements.py:74`).

**Tests:**

Status: draft for the author's review. Nothing is implemented until it is approved.

table and fencing), PR #8 (Kafka delivery and the reconciler) and PR #9 (Stage 4). What spec
§11 still lists as planned:
- the real pipeline in the worker (today it runs `SimulatedPipeline`);
- the recovery experiments E1/E2;
- the Redis result cache;
- the cache experiment E3;
- their documentation.

This plan turns the author's six-point outline into milestones M1–M6, one branch and one PR
each. Each milestone has:
- deliverables;
- acceptance criteria;
- tests;
- a statement of how it keeps the guarantee.

Four cross-cutting requirements run through all of them:
- code provenance for `jobs/`;
- reproducible dependencies;
- startup commands;
- measured memory budgets.

Data verification, the privacy-hook fixes and AI-log review stay in separate workstreams.

State observed on 2026-10-23:
- **Main worktree.** It is on `fix/measure-process-kinds` (97c35f3). That branch is pushed but

## Ground rules for every milestone

1. **The guarantee** (spec §11): each job accepts at most one result, every succeeded job has
   exactly one, and a job may execute more than once.
   - **Enforcement.** Only the token-guarded UPDATEs in `jobs/store.py` enforce it. The existing
     `INVARIANT_QUERIES` and `JobStore.invariant_violations()` (store.py:127, :481) check it.
     Together, the first two queries forbid a second accepted attempt for any job.
   - **Accepting.** Nothing but `JobStore.accept_result` may produce an accepted attempt.
   - **Cleanup** never touches an accepted attempt's folder.
   - **The cache** reads accepted runs only and never writes the job table.
   - **Checking.** `invariant_violations()` must be empty after every test scenario, every
     worker run and every experiment batch.
2. **Authorship** (spec §11, "Stages and authorship"). Claude Code writes:
   - the Compose services;
   - the worker integration;
   - the CLIs;
   - the injection and measurement tooling;

   like `docs/partition-experiment.md:3-5`, reworded for the tutored model.
3. **Review gates.** Each milestone opens with a findings report; nothing is fixed before the
   author has read it. Each closes with a stop for review before the PR is merged.
4. **Git.**
   - **Isolation.** Each milestone gets its own worktree (`.claude/worktrees/<name>`) from an
     up-to-date `main`, so the main worktree's W2 changes never enter a milestone branch.
   - **Staging and merging.** Stage files by explicit path only. Merge with merge commits,
     never squash or rebase. Every commit ends with the Co-Authored-By trailer.
   - **AI logs.** Milestone commits contain no AI logs; those go to W3.
   - **PRs.** Claude pushes the branch; the author opens and merges the PR on GitHub.
   - **Formal sessions** run on a merged, clean commit whose SHA lands in every record. There
     are no commits during a session.
5. **Privacy.** `data/` and the private plan stay out of Git. Memory files,
   `.git/info/exclude` and app lists are never printed in tool calls. Batch folders live under

6. **Measurement sessions.** While one runs, other sessions only write and review. They wait

7. **Wording.** Use explicit counts. Claim nothing beyond what was measured. Write "one

Order: M1 → M2 → M3 and M1 → M4 → M5, then M6. M4 does not need M2 or M3, because it can use

### M2 — The worker runs windows → spark_pipeline → verify
Branch `feature/worker-pipeline` · Author: Claude Code (spec §11) · Depends on M1.

**Design.** The new code is `jobs/pipeline.py`, `jobs/launcher.py`, `jobs/params.py`,
`jobs/events.py` and `jobs/__main__.py`, plus small changes to `worker.py` and `kafka.py`. The
store's guards stay as they are.

**Job parameters (`params.py`).**
- **Schema.** A frozen dataclass: snapshot, kind (`rolling` / `calendar-year` / `full-period`),
  window days, stride, anchor, sample ticker. Unknown keys are refused. Tickers come from the
  snapshot, and leverages are fixed at 1x and 2x.
- **Input checksums.** `submit` computes `input_checksums` from the files that `windows.py`
  records in `inputs_sha256`: `daily_returns/*.parquet` and `quality_report.json`.
- **Check before running.** The worker re-checks them before step 1. A mismatch fails the attempt
  as not retryable.

**Steps.** Each step runs as `sys.executable -m etf_risk.<module>` with absolute paths only.
Everything lands inside the attempt folder:
1. `windows --out-root <run_dir>/windows --name <name>` writes
   `<run_dir>/windows/<snapshot>/<name>/`.
2. `spark_pipeline --windows … --out-root <run_dir>/output --run-id <run id>` writes
   `<run_dir>/output/<snapshot>/<name>/<run id>/`.
3. `verify --run …` checks that output.

Setup for every step:
- the working directory, `TMPDIR`, `SPARK_LOCAL_DIRS` and `java.io.tmpdir` all point to
  `<run_dir>/.work`;
- logs go to `<run_dir>/logs/<step>.log`.

**Result rule.**
- **When the worker accepts.** Every step exits 0, `run.json` has status `ok`, every
  `checks.json` count is 0, `verify.json` has no mismatch and the same breached windows, and
  every table has `_SUCCESS`.
- **Then.** `.work` is removed and the worker calls `accept_result`.

**Failure classification.** This is decided from the records, not the exit code alone.
- **Not retryable:**
  - a checksum error (exit 3);
  - `run.json` status `checks_failed`;
  - a verify mismatch;
  - a parameter or input-checksum error.
- **Retryable:**
  - a signal;
  - a timeout;
  - status `failed`;
  - a missing record.

Retryable failures go back to the queue until `max_attempts` (3).

**Heartbeats.**
- **Where.** The worker thread waits on the child with `wait(timeout=…)` and calls `heartbeat()`
  every lease/4 (15 s at the 60 s default). There is no background thread, so the database
  connection stays on one thread.
- **Failed renewals.** A renewal that raises (database unreachable) is retried at the next tick.
  When the time since the last successful renewal reaches the lease minus a margin, the worker
  fences itself: it kills the run and raises `Fenced`. Two Spark runs on one machine would risk
  memory, and the token guard still decides acceptance.

**Fencing.** When `heartbeat()` returns false, the worker sends SIGTERM to the step's process
group, waits a grace period, sends SIGKILL, and raises `Fenced`. The folder stays and is never
referenced.

**Timeouts.**
- **Limits.** Each step and the whole attempt get a wall-clock limit. Draft values are 120 s,
  600 s, 300 s and 900 s, against measured medians of a few seconds, 18–47 s and about 14 s;
  they are fixed at review from M2's measurements.
- **On timeout.** The process group is killed and the attempt fails as retryable.
- **Kafka settings.** `max.poll.interval.ms` (above the attempt limit) and `session.timeout.ms`
  are set in `kafka.py` and pinned by tests.

**Cleanup.**
- **Lifeline.** Each step starts in a new process group behind `launcher.py`, which holds a
  "lifeline" pipe from the worker. If the worker dies, even by SIGKILL, the launcher reads EOF
  and kills its group. macOS has no parent-death signal.
- **Stale groups.** Each attempt writes its group id to `.work/pgid`. On startup, a worker kills
  the groups that a previous worker left unfinished.
- **`jobs cleanup`** is a dry run unless given `--delete`. It removes folders of failed or expired
  attempts that ended more than a grace period ago. Folders with no attempt row are only
  reported. It never touches accepted or running attempts.

**Graceful stop.** On SIGTERM or SIGINT the worker stops polling, kills the running step and
calls `fail_attempt(retryable=True)`, so the job is requeued at once.

**Event log (`events.py`).** Each process appends JSON lines with UTC times, one flushed line per
event:
- delivered
- claimed
- renewed and renewal failed
- step start and end
- fenced
- accepted
- failed
- requeued
- published

E2's timings come from these logs plus the tables, without a new table.

**CLI** `python -m etf_risk.jobs`:
- `init-db`
- `create-topic`
- `submit`
- `worker`
- `reconciler`
- `cleanup`
- `status [--check]`, which prints the tables and `invariant_violations()` and exits 1 on a
  violation

Flags or `ETF_RISK_MYSQL_URL` and `ETF_RISK_KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP` configure it, and logging is set up.

**Attempt record.** `attempt.json` holds the worker id, run id, steps (exit code, times), the
input checksums as checked and `code_state()`.

**Optional defense in depth.** A unique index on accepted attempts per job: a partial index in
SQLite, and in MySQL a unique index on a generated column that is `job_id` only when the
outcome is accepted. The schema-drift test is updated, and a test shows that a second accepted
row is refused.

**Deliverables.** The modules above; updated `job-queue.md` (real pipeline, settings table,
known limits resolved); the runbook's E1/E2 section; budget rows for the worker, reconciler and
submit.

**Acceptance.** Native worker, MySQL and Kafka in Compose, on fresh containers:
- **Normal runs.** A calendar-year job and a stride-21 job of `full-2026-10-12` each end
  `succeeded`, with exactly one accepted attempt that passes every check and verify. Their
  content equals a direct CLI run under the `compare_tables` rules
  (analysis/collect_partition_measurements.py:286, partition-experiment.md:476-515).
- **Stalled worker.** After SIGSTOP for longer than the lease, a standby worker takes over. On
  SIGCONT the stalled worker's process tree is gone within the grace period, it writes nothing
  more, and the takeover's result is accepted.
- **Crashed worker.** After SIGKILL during step 2, no Spark process is left once the lifeline
  grace has passed, and the job is requeued after its lease and succeeds.
- **Timeout.** An attempt that exceeds its limit is killed and retried.
- **Temp files.** No new `spark-*` or `blockmgr-*` folder appears in `/tmp` or `$TMPDIR`.
- **Cleanup dry run.** It lists exactly the failed and expired attempts.
- **Peaks.** Measured and within budget.
- **Invariants.** `invariant_violations()` is empty throughout.
- **Earlier tests.** Every earlier job test still passes on both stores.

**Tests.**
- **`test_jobs_pipeline.py`** (offline, with fake step scripts): heartbeat cadence; fencing kills
  the group (checked with psutil); timeouts; failure classification; the lifeline (kill the
  parent, the grandchild dies); `.work` cleanup; parameter and checksum refusals.
- **CLI and cleanup tests.**
- **A Spark-marked end-to-end test:** a tiny job through `Worker` with SQLite and `MemoryQueue`.
- **A live end-to-end test** gated by the environment variables: real worker and reconciler

**Guarantee.** Acceptance still goes only through the token guard. Fencing and self-fencing
only stop work. Cleanup excludes accepted attempts. The optional index makes a second accepted
row impossible at the storage level.

### M3 — Recovery experiments E1 and E2
Branch `feature/recovery-experiment` · Tooling: Claude Code · Experiment: the project author,
tutored · Depends on M2.

**Claude's tooling (first commit, with tests).**
- **Crash injection.** Crashes at the existing worker fault points (`Worker(fault=…)`,

**The author's `docs/recovery-experiment.md`.** Claude scaffolds the headings of Parts A and B
(sections 1–15 and History) and the `Author:` line.
- **Part A, decided by the author:**
  - the cases;
  - repetitions;
  - lease, heartbeat and reconcile settings;
  - the job size (calendar-year vs stride 21, with the memory implications in D);
  - metric definitions;
  - predictions;
  - acceptance criteria;
  - stop rules;
  - one fresh MySQL container per batch.

  - worker crash before the claim;
  - crash after the claim but before the acknowledgement (the job-9 timeline);
  - crash during step 2;
  - crash after the pipeline but before acceptance;
  - crash after acceptance;
  - a stalled worker taken over, then fenced;
  - Kafka restart while idle, during a submit, and during a run;
  - MySQL restart during a run, shorter and longer than the lease;
  - MySQL restart at acceptance (the failed-COMMIT path).
- **Metrics per job:**
  - injection time;
  - detection: the expired attempt's `ended_at`, or the requeue or redelivery event;
  - recovery: the next `claimed_at`;
  - completion: `finished_at`;
  - executions;

`test_caching_session.py`, including planted problems that each fail their criterion; tests of

### M4 — Redis cache for summary queries, with fallback
Branch `feature/result-cache` · Infrastructure: Claude Code · Cache logic: the project author,
tutored · Depends on M1.

Setup for every step:

  `<run_dir>/.work`;
- logs go to `<run_dir>/logs/<step>.log`.

**Result rule.**
- **When the worker accepts.** Every step exits 0, `run.json` has status `ok`, every
  `checks.json` count is 0, `verify.json` has no mismatch and the same breached windows, and
  every table has `_SUCCESS`.
- **Then.** `.work` is removed and the worker calls `accept_result`.

**Failure classification.** This is decided from the records, not the exit code alone.
- **Not retryable:**
  - a checksum error (exit 3);
  - `run.json` status `checks_failed`;
  - a verify mismatch;
  - a parameter or input-checksum error.
- **Retryable:**
  - a signal;
  - a timeout;
  - status `failed`;
  - a missing record.

Retryable failures go back to the queue until `max_attempts` (3).

**Heartbeats.**
- **Where.** The worker thread waits on the child with `wait(timeout=…)` and calls `heartbeat()`
  every lease/4 (15 s at the 60 s default). There is no background thread, so the database
  connection stays on one thread.
- **Failed renewals.** A renewal that raises (database unreachable) is retried at the next tick.
  When the time since the last successful renewal reaches the lease minus a margin, the worker
  fences itself: it kills the run and raises `Fenced`. Two Spark runs on one machine would risk
  memory, and the token guard still decides acceptance.

**Fencing.** When `heartbeat()` returns false, the worker sends SIGTERM to the step's process
group, waits a grace period, sends SIGKILL, and raises `Fenced`. The folder stays and is never
referenced.

**Timeouts.**
- **Limits.** Each step and the whole attempt get a wall-clock limit. Draft values are 120 s,
  600 s, 300 s and 900 s, against measured medians of a few seconds, 18–47 s and about 14 s;
  they are fixed at review from M2's measurements.
- **On timeout.** The process group is killed and the attempt fails as retryable.
- **Kafka settings.** `max.poll.interval.ms` (above the attempt limit) and `session.timeout.ms`
  are set in `kafka.py` and pinned by tests.

**Cleanup.**
- **Lifeline.** Each step starts in a new process group behind `launcher.py`, which holds a
  "lifeline" pipe from the worker. If the worker dies, even by SIGKILL, the launcher reads EOF
  and kills its group. macOS has no parent-death signal.
- **Stale groups.** Each attempt writes its group id to `.work/pgid`. On startup, a worker kills
  the groups that a previous worker left unfinished.
- **`jobs cleanup`** is a dry run unless given `--delete`. It removes folders of failed or expired
  attempts that ended more than a grace period ago. Folders with no attempt row are only
  reported. It never touches accepted or running attempts.

**Graceful stop.** On SIGTERM or SIGINT the worker stops polling, kills the running step and
calls `fail_attempt(retryable=True)`, so the job is requeued at once.

**Event log (`events.py`).** Each process appends JSON lines with UTC times, one flushed line per
event:
- delivered
- claimed
- renewed and renewal failed
- step start and end
- fenced
- accepted
- failed
- requeued
- published

- `create-topic`

- `worker`
