## Running

Requires Python 3.12, Java 17 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/); run the
commands from the repository root. Memory use has been measured on one machine
only (see Key results): there, runs at strides 21 to 7 peaked at 1.2 to 2.8 GiB,
and the exploratory stride-3 runs at up to 2.8 GiB; other machines, and Spark
settings beyond the shuffle-partition experiment's three, have not been
measured.

```bash
uv sync                                    # .venv from uv.lock
uv run --group measure --group plots pytest  # tests, no network

# 1. Download a snapshot (network). Set SNAPSHOT once; the later steps use it.
SNAPSHOT=full-$(date +%Y-%m-%d)
uv run --group download python -m etf_risk.download \
    --tickers NVDA AAPL MSFT TSLA QQQ --out data/raw/yahoo/$SNAPSHOT
# 2. Check the prices, then write daily returns       -> data/processed/$SNAPSHOT/
uv run python -m etf_risk.ingest --raw-dir data/raw/yahoo/$SNAPSHOT
# 3. Define 252-day windows at stride 21              -> data/windows/$SNAPSHOT/rolling-252-s21/
uv run python -m etf_risk.windows --snapshot $SNAPSHOT --kind rolling --stride 21
# 4. Run the model in Spark; every check runs at full scale -> $RUN
RUN=data/outputs/windows/$SNAPSHOT/rolling-252-s21/first
uv run python -m etf_risk.spark_pipeline --windows data/windows/$SNAPSHOT/rolling-252-s21 --run-id first
# 5. Compare a sample of windows with an independent Python computation
uv run python -m etf_risk.verify --run $RUN
# 6. The three SQL analyses of the run
uv run python analysis/sql_overview.py $RUN
uv run python analysis/sql_comparison.py $RUN
uv run python analysis/sql_sensitivity.py $RUN
# 7. The figures of this run; X1-X4 read the committed CSVs -> data/figures-$SNAPSHOT/
uv run --group plots python -m etf_risk.plots --run $RUN --snapshot data/processed/$SNAPSHOT \
    --windows data/windows/$SNAPSHOT/rolling-252-s21 --out data/figures-$SNAPSHOT
```

Optional steps, with the same variables:

```bash
# Calendar-year windows, a labeled supplement
uv run python -m etf_risk.windows --snapshot $SNAPSHOT --kind calendar-year
uv run python -m etf_risk.spark_pipeline --windows data/windows/$SNAPSHOT/calendar-year --run-id first
# Timed runs with peak memory: a fresh process per run; no further run once 60% of RAM is crossed
uv run --group measure python -m etf_risk.measure --repeats 4 -- --windows data/windows/$SNAPSHOT/rolling-252-s21
```

- Unless `--end` is changed, the download stops at 2025-12-31, the same range as
  the run of record. Yahoo can revise adjusted prices, so a new snapshot can
  differ slightly ([data-sources.md](docs/data-sources.md)).
- Nothing is overwritten: `windows` refuses an existing folder (unless
  `--overwrite`), and `spark_pipeline` asks for a new `--run-id`.
- `spark_pipeline` also takes `--shuffle-partitions N` and `--coalesce on|off`
  (Spark settings, refused inside an existing Spark session) and
  `--record-plans`, which writes `plans.json` with the run's final plans and
  the partition counts Spark used
  ([partition-experiment.md](docs/partition-experiment.md) 4).
- `spark_pipeline --cache none|members|members-checks` caches the
  window-member rows, or those and the four read-back tables, and records the
  fills, releases and Spark's storage information in `run.json`
  ([caching-experiment.md](docs/caching-experiment.md) 4).
- `etf_risk.pandas_pipeline` takes `--windows`, `--out-root` and `--run-id`
  and writes the Spark pipeline's outputs from one process, without Spark;
  `etf_risk.measure --pipeline pandas` times it
  ([pandas-baseline.md](docs/pandas-baseline.md) 4).
- Strides below 21 need `--allow-dense-stride`. Strides 14, 7 and 3 were
  measured in the stride experiment (stride 3 as exploratory only); stride 1
  has not been run.
- The 2020–2025 prototype regression needs the prototype CSVs, which were
  downloaded outside this repository ([data-sources.md](docs/data-sources.md)).
- `etf_risk.plots` draws the figures of [docs/results.md](docs/results.md).
  X1–X4 read the experiments' measurement CSVs, committed in
  [docs/measurements](docs/measurements/README.md), so they also work from a
  fresh clone (`--figures X1 X2 X3 X4`). An input that is missing, cannot be
  parsed or lacks a column the figures read is named, and nothing is drawn;
  `--check` compares the numbers with the documented values and says which
  figures it could not compare ([docs/demo.md](docs/demo.md)).

### Docker

The image holds the code, Python 3.12, Java 17 and the locked dependencies. Data
is never copied into it: `docker/run.sh` mounts `data/processed` and
`data/windows` read-only and writes container results to `data/outputs-docker`
and `data/windows-docker`, apart from native results. Keep the image local; do
not push it.

```bash
docker/build.sh            # builds etf-risk:dev; records the commit and whether src/, pyproject.toml, uv.lock were clean
docker/run.sh              # the test suite in the container (the transcript-hook tests stay native)
# Steps 4-5 in the container, on the definitions from step 3
docker/run.sh python -m etf_risk.spark_pipeline --windows data/windows/$SNAPSHOT/rolling-252-s21 \
    --out-root data/outputs-docker/windows --run-id first
docker/run.sh python -m etf_risk.verify --run data/outputs-docker/windows/$SNAPSHOT/rolling-252-s21/first
```

The SQL analyses run natively on a container run's folder as well. The image
has no `.git`, so run records take the commit and clean flag from the build
(`code_source: "build"`) and the image ID from `docker/run.sh`; `source_sha256`
still identifies the code. `docker/run.sh` sets a memory limit
(`ETF_RISK_MEMORY`, default `2.5g`, a budget to validate) with no swap and
prints the container's cgroup memory peak, which includes page cache. Timings
in the container (a Linux VM on macOS, data on bind mounts) are a separate
configuration, not comparable with native measurements.

## Data

Daily prices come from Yahoo Finance through yfinance and are not committed

- `spark_pipeline --cache none|members|members-checks` caches the
  window-member rows, or those and the four read-back tables, and records the
  fills, releases and Spark's storage information in `run.json`
  ([caching-experiment.md](docs/caching-experiment.md) 4).
- `etf_risk.pandas_pipeline` takes `--windows`, `--out-root` and `--run-id`
  and writes the Spark pipeline's outputs from one process, without Spark;
  `etf_risk.measure --pipeline pandas` times it
  ([pandas-baseline.md](docs/pandas-baseline.md) 4).
- Strides below 21 need `--allow-dense-stride`. Strides 14, 7 and 3 were
  measured in the stride experiment (stride 3 as exploratory only); stride 1
  has not been run.
- The 2020–2025 prototype regression needs the prototype CSVs, which were
  downloaded outside this repository ([data-sources.md](docs/data-sources.md)).
- `etf_risk.plots` draws the figures of [docs/results.md](docs/results.md).
  X1–X4 read the experiments' measurement CSVs, committed in
  [docs/measurements](docs/measurements/README.md), so they also work from a
  fresh clone (`--figures X1 X2 X3 X4`). An input that is missing, cannot be
  parsed or lacks a column the figures read is named, and nothing is drawn;
  `--check` compares the numbers with the documented values and says which
  figures it could not compare ([docs/demo.md](docs/demo.md)).

### Docker

The image holds the code, Python 3.12, Java 17 and the locked dependencies. Data
is never copied into it: `docker/run.sh` mounts `data/processed` and
`data/windows` read-only and writes container results to `data/outputs-docker`
and `data/windows-docker`, apart from native results. Keep the image local; do
not push it.

```bash
docker/build.sh            # builds etf-risk:dev; records the commit and whether src/, pyproject.toml, uv.lock were clean
docker/run.sh              # the test suite in the container (the transcript-hook tests stay native)
# Steps 4-5 in the container, on the definitions from step 3
docker/run.sh python -m etf_risk.spark_pipeline --windows data/windows/$SNAPSHOT/rolling-252-s21 \
    --out-root data/outputs-docker/windows --run-id first
docker/run.sh python -m etf_risk.verify --run data/outputs-docker/windows/$SNAPSHOT/rolling-252-s21/first
```

The SQL analyses run natively on a container run's folder as well. The image
has no `.git`, so run records take the commit and clean flag from the build
(`code_source: "build"`) and the image ID from `docker/run.sh`; `source_sha256`
still identifies the code. `docker/run.sh` sets a memory limit
(`ETF_RISK_MEMORY`, default `2.5g`, a budget to validate) with no swap and
prints the container's cgroup memory peak, which includes page cache. Timings
in the container (a Linux VM on macOS, data on bind mounts) are a separate
configuration, not comparable with native measurements.

class Pass:

    failed: int = 0         # expired leases with no attempts left

    unconfirmed: int = 0    # publications not confirmed; the next pass tries again
    waiting: int = 0        # never-claimed jobs still within the grace period
    stale: int = 0          # jobs that changed between the read and the change: left alone

            raise ValueError(f"the publication grace ({publication_grace}) must exceed the confirmation timeout"
                             f" ({confirmation_timeout}), or the reconciler races a submitter still waiting")

        self.publisher = publisher
        self.publication_grace = publication_grace

        done = Pass()
        for lease in self.store.expired_leases():
            status = self.store.requeue_expired(lease.job_id, lease.token)
            if status is Status.QUEUED:
                done.requeued += 1
            elif status is Status.FAILED:
                done.failed += 1
            else:
                done.stale += 1

                done.unconfirmed += 1

                done.published += 1
            else:
                done.stale += 1
        return done

        """Pass after pass until stop is set. A pass that raises is logged, and the next one
        starts after the interval."""
        while not stop.is_set():
            try:
                done = self.run_once()

import logging
from datetime import timedelta

from etf_risk.jobs.queue import CONFIRMATION_TIMEOUT, Delivery, encode

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def producer_config(bootstrap: str, *, confirmation_timeout: timedelta = CONFIRMATION_TIMEOUT) -> dict:
    return {"bootstrap.servers": bootstrap, "acks": "all", "enable.idempotence": True, "linger.ms": 0,
            "message.timeout.ms": int(confirmation_timeout.total_seconds() * 1000)}


def consumer_config(bootstrap: str, group: str) -> dict:
    return {"bootstrap.servers": bootstrap, "group.id": group, "enable.auto.commit": False,
            "enable.auto.offset.store": False, "auto.offset.reset": "earliest"}


class KafkaPublisher:
    def __init__(self, bootstrap: str, topic: str, *, confirmation_timeout: timedelta = CONFIRMATION_TIMEOUT):
        from confluent_kafka import Producer
        self.topic = topic
        self._wait = confirmation_timeout.total_seconds() + 1.0   # the report comes by the message timeout
        self._producer = Producer({**producer_config(bootstrap, confirmation_timeout=confirmation_timeout),
                                   "logger": log})

    def publish(self, job_id: int) -> bool:
        """Send the job id and wait for the broker's confirmation. True only if it arrived;
        False may still mean the message was written and its confirmation lost."""
        from confluent_kafka import KafkaException
        report: dict = {}
        try:
            self._producer.produce(self.topic, key=encode(job_id), value=encode(job_id),
                                   on_delivery=lambda error, message: report.setdefault("error", error))
        except (BufferError, KafkaException):
            log.warning("could not send job %s", job_id, exc_info=True)
            return False
        self._producer.flush(self._wait)
        if report.get("error") is not None:
            log.warning("job %s: publication not confirmed: %s", job_id, report["error"])
        return "error" in report and report["error"] is None

"""Record which code produced a result, including uncommitted changes.

A git commit alone does not identify the code when the worktree has changes, so
code_state() also records whether the worktree is clean and the SHA-256 of every
module in src/etf_risk/ and of uv.lock.

The Docker image has no .git: there the commit and the clean flag come from what
docker/build.sh recorded at build time (code_source = "build"), and docker/run.sh
passes the image ID.

AI contribution: written with Claude Code (Opus 5.5). Verified with
tests/test_spark_equivalence.py (run.json carries these fields) and tests/test_provenance.py.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

from etf_risk.ingest import sha256_file

PACKAGE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
REPO_ROOT = PACKAGE_DIR.parents[1]

# Set in the Docker image (Dockerfile, from docker/build.sh) and by docker/run.sh.
BUILD_COMMIT_ENV = "ETF_RISK_GIT_COMMIT"
BUILD_CLEAN_ENV = "ETF_RISK_GIT_WORKTREE_CLEAN"
IMAGE_ID_ENV = "ETF_RISK_IMAGE_ID"


def resolve(path: str | Path) -> Path:
    """Paths stored in configs are relative to the repository root unless absolute."""
    path = Path(path)
    return path if path.is_absolute() else REPO_ROOT / path


def _git(*args: str) -> str | None:
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(REPO_ROOT), *args], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
        return None
    return out.stdout.strip() if out.returncode == 0 else None


def code_state() -> dict:
    head = _git("rev-parse", "HEAD")
    status = _git("status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=all", "--", "src", "pyproject.toml", "uv.lock")
    if head:
        source, commit, clean = "git", head, (status == "") if status is not None else None
    elif os.environ.get(BUILD_COMMIT_ENV):
        source, commit = "build", os.environ[BUILD_COMMIT_ENV]
        clean = {"true": True, "false": False}.get(os.environ.get(BUILD_CLEAN_ENV, "").lower())
    else:
        source, commit, clean = "unknown", "unknown", None
    lock = REPO_ROOT / "uv.lock"
    return {
        "git_commit": commit,
        # False means the code that ran is not exactly the recorded commit; source_sha256 identifies it.
        "git_worktree_clean": clean,
        "code_source": source,
        "image_id": os.environ.get(IMAGE_ID_ENV) or None,
        "source_sha256": {p.name: sha256_file(p) for p in sorted(PACKAGE_DIR.glob("*.py"))},
        "uv_lock_sha256": sha256_file(lock) if lock.is_file() else None,
    }

"""Record which code produced a result, including uncommitted changes.

A git commit alone does not identify the code when the worktree has changes, so
code_state() also records whether the worktree is clean and the SHA-256 of uv.lock and
of every Python module and SQL schema under src/etf_risk/, subpackages included (the
job queue in jobs/ and its schema files). Keys are paths relative to src/etf_risk/, so a
top-level module keeps the key it always had ("model.py") and jobs/__init__.py does not
collide with __init__.py. Records written before 2026-10-23 hash the top-level modules
only.

The Docker image has no .git: there the commit and the clean flag come from what
docker/build.sh recorded at build time (code_source = "build"), and docker/run.sh
passes the image ID.

AI contribution: written with Claude Code (Opus 5.5). Verified with
tests/test_spark_equivalence.py (run.json carries these fields) and tests/test_provenance.py.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

from etf_risk.ingest import sha256_file

PACKAGE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
REPO_ROOT = PACKAGE_DIR.parents[1]
SOURCE_SUFFIXES = (".py", ".sql")

# Set in the Docker image (Dockerfile, from docker/build.sh) and by docker/run.sh.
BUILD_COMMIT_ENV = "ETF_RISK_GIT_COMMIT"
BUILD_CLEAN_ENV = "ETF_RISK_GIT_WORKTREE_CLEAN"
IMAGE_ID_ENV = "ETF_RISK_IMAGE_ID"


def resolve(path: str | Path) -> Path:
    """Paths stored in configs are relative to the repository root unless absolute."""
    path = Path(path)
    return path if path.is_absolute() else REPO_ROOT / path


def _git(*args: str) -> str | None:
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(REPO_ROOT), *args], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
        return None
    return out.stdout.strip() if out.returncode == 0 else None


def source_files() -> dict[str, Path]:
    """Every Python module and SQL schema of the package, by path relative to it."""
    files = (p for p in PACKAGE_DIR.rglob("*") if p.suffix in SOURCE_SUFFIXES and p.is_file())
    return {p.relative_to(PACKAGE_DIR).as_posix(): p for p in sorted(files)}


def code_state() -> dict:
    head = _git("rev-parse", "HEAD")
    status = _git("status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=all", "--", "src", "pyproject.toml", "uv.lock")
    if head:
        source, commit, clean = "git", head, (status == "") if status is not None else None
    elif os.environ.get(BUILD_COMMIT_ENV):
        source, commit = "build", os.environ[BUILD_COMMIT_ENV]
        clean = {"true": True, "false": False}.get(os.environ.get(BUILD_CLEAN_ENV, "").lower())
    else:
        source, commit, clean = "unknown", "unknown", None
    lock = REPO_ROOT / "uv.lock"
    return {
        "git_commit": commit,
        # False means the code that ran is not exactly the recorded commit; source_sha256 identifies it.
        "git_worktree_clean": clean,
        "code_source": source,
        "image_id": os.environ.get(IMAGE_ID_ENV) or None,
        "source_sha256": {p.name: sha256_file(p) for p in sorted(PACKAGE_DIR.glob("*.py"))},
        "uv_lock_sha256": sha256_file(lock) if lock.is_file() else None,
    }

# Services of the systems extension (spec §11), each with the spec's memory budget and
# reachable from this machine only; name the services a run needs. Nothing else in the
# project starts them.
# - mysql: the job table. A 64 MiB buffer pool, performance_schema off, a 512 MiB container
#   without swap.
# - kafka: the job queue. One KRaft node that is broker and controller, with a 256 MiB heap
#   in a 640 MiB container without swap. Clients on this machine use 127.0.0.1:9094;
#   containers on this Compose network will use kafka:9092. Topics are not created on
#   first use: create them with etf_risk.jobs.kafka.create_topic().
#
#   docker compose -f docker/compose.yaml up -d --wait mysql kafka
#   ETF_RISK_MYSQL_URL=mysql://root:jobs-test@127.0.0.1:3307 ETF_RISK_KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP=127.0.0.1:9094 \
#       uv run --with 'pymysql[rsa]==1.1.1' --with 'confluent-kafka==2.16.0' python -m pytest tests/test_jobs_*.py
#   docker compose -f docker/compose.yaml down -v        # removes the data volumes as well
#
# The tests create and drop a database and a topic of their own for each test. The root
# password is a fixed test value for a server listening on 127.0.0.1 only;
# ETF_RISK_MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD overrides it. Both images are pinned by digest, as pulled on
# 2026-10-22 (docker image inspect --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' <image>): MySQL 8.4.13
# from the 8.4 LTS line, and Kafka 4.3.1, the newest release that was at least two weeks old.
#
# AI contribution: written with Claude Code (Opus 5.5).
name: etf-risk-jobs
services:
  mysql:
    image: mysql:8.4.13@sha256:76f0358884cb92d9a086d24e5671c38048d3fef40f2588703d73eb55392d6b69
    command: ["--innodb-buffer-pool-size=64M", "--performance-schema=OFF"]
    environment:
      MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${ETF_RISK_MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD:-jobs-test}
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:3307:3306"
    mem_limit: 512m
    memswap_limit: 512m
    healthcheck:
      # Answers once the server accepts TCP connections, even before a login succeeds.
      test: ["CMD", "mysqladmin", "ping", "--host=127.0.0.1", "--silent"]
      interval: 2s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 60

  kafka:
    image: apache/kafka:4.3.1@sha256:77e3df9054047a88b520d0cc46e16696d3b22022e1d580aeccd2632df6532837
    environment:
      KAFKA_NODE_ID: 1
      KAFKA_PROCESS_ROLES: broker,controller
      KAFKA_LISTENERS: INTERNAL://:9092,HOST://:9094,CONTROLLER://:9093
      KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS: INTERNAL://kafka:9092,HOST://127.0.0.1:9094
      KAFKA_LISTENER_SECURITY_PROTOCOL_MAP: INTERNAL:PLAINTEXT,HOST:PLAINTEXT,CONTROLLER:PLAINTEXT
      KAFKA_INTER_BROKER_LISTENER_NAME: INTERNAL
      KAFKA_CONTROLLER_LISTENER_NAMES: CONTROLLER
      KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS: 1@localhost:9093
      KAFKA_OFFSETS_TOPIC_REPLICATION_FACTOR: 1          # one broker: no replicas
      KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_REPLICATION_FACTOR: 1
      KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_MIN_ISR: 1
      KAFKA_GROUP_INITIAL_REBALANCE_DELAY_MS: 0          # a new consumer group starts at once
      KAFKA_AUTO_CREATE_TOPICS_ENABLE: "false"
      KAFKA_HEAP_OPTS: -Xms256m -Xmx256m
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:9094:9094"
    mem_limit: 640m
    memswap_limit: 640m
    healthcheck:
      # A port check (BusyBox nc), so no second JVM starts inside the memory limit.
      test: ["CMD", "nc", "-z", "localhost", "9094"]
      interval: 2s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 60

Offline, always: the producer's and the consumer's settings (acks=all, idempotence, the
message timeout equal to the confirmation timeout; no auto-commit, earliest).
Against Kafka (skipped unless ETF_RISK_KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP is set), each test on a topic of
its own (KafkaTopic, tests/jobs_backends.py):
- jobs published before a fresh consumer group starts are all delivered, and with latest,
  librdkafka's default, the same group would get none of them;
- publish() returns True once the broker confirmed, and False for an unreachable broker;
- an uncommitted message reaches the group's next consumer, a committed one does not;
- a rewind delivers the same message again;
- end to end, submit_job(), Worker.serve() and the reconciler, with the job table on SQLite
  and, with ETF_RISK_MYSQL_URL set, on MySQL; an oversized payload ahead of a job is
  committed and skipped; after a persistent error before the acknowledgement, serve()
  gives up with the message uncommitted, for a restarted worker.

    docker compose -f docker/compose.yaml up -d --wait kafka mysql
    ETF_RISK_KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP=127.0.0.1:9094 ETF_RISK_MYSQL_URL=mysql://root:jobs-test@127.0.0.1:3307 \\
        uv run --with 'confluent-kafka==2.16.0' --with 'pymysql[rsa]==1.1.1' python -m pytest tests/test_jobs_*.py
    docker compose -f docker/compose.yaml down -v

"""
import time
from datetime import timedelta

import pytest

from etf_risk.jobs.kafka import consumer_config, producer_config
from etf_risk.jobs.queue import CONFIRMATION_TIMEOUT, submit_job
from etf_risk.jobs.reconciler import Pass, Reconciler
from etf_risk.jobs.simulated import SimulatedCrash
from etf_risk.jobs.store import Refusal, Status
from etf_risk.jobs.worker import Result, Served
from jobs_backends import (BACKENDS, LEASE, PARAMS, KafkaTopic, WorkerEnv, failing_at, make_backend, needs_kafka,
                           poll_after_assignment, poll_deliveries)


# Offline

def test_the_producer_waits_for_the_broker_and_is_idempotent():
    config = producer_config("broker:9092")
    assert (config["acks"], config["enable.idempotence"]) == ("all", True)
    assert config["message.timeout.ms"] == CONFIRMATION_TIMEOUT.total_seconds() * 1000 == 10_000


def test_the_consumer_commits_only_when_told_and_a_new_group_starts_at_the_earliest_message():
    config = consumer_config("broker:9092", "workers")
    assert (config["group.id"], config["enable.auto.commit"], config["enable.auto.offset.store"],
            config["auto.offset.reset"]) == ("workers", False, False, "earliest")


def test_an_unreachable_broker_gives_false():
    pytest.importorskip("confluent_kafka")
    from etf_risk.jobs.kafka import KafkaPublisher
    publisher = KafkaPublisher("127.0.0.1:1", "nowhere", confirmation_timeout=timedelta(seconds=2))
    started = time.monotonic()
    assert publisher.publish(1) is False
    assert time.monotonic() - started < 10


# Against Kafka

@pytest.fixture
def topic():
    topic = KafkaTopic()
    yield topic
    topic.close()


@needs_kafka
def test_jobs_published_before_a_fresh_group_starts_are_all_delivered(topic):
    publisher = topic.publisher()
    assert all(publisher.publish(job) for job in (1, 2, 3))
    consumer = topic.consumer(topic.group())                        # a group that never existed
    assert [d.job_id() for d in poll_deliveries(consumer, 3)] == [1, 2, 3]


@needs_kafka
def test_with_latest_a_fresh_group_would_miss_them(topic):
    publisher = topic.publisher()
    assert all(publisher.publish(job) for job in (1, 2, 3))
    consumer = topic.consumer(topic.group(), settings={"auto.offset.reset": "latest"})
    assert poll_after_assignment(consumer) == []


@needs_kafka
def test_a_confirmed_message_is_there_when_publish_returns(topic):
    assert topic.publisher().publish(7)
    [delivery] = poll_deliveries(topic.consumer(topic.group()), 1)
    assert delivery.job_id() == 7 and delivery.position == (topic.name, 0, 0)


@needs_kafka
def test_an_uncommitted_message_reaches_the_groups_next_consumer_and_a_committed_one_does_not(topic):
    assert topic.publisher().publish(5)
    group = topic.group()
    first = topic.consumer(group)
    [delivery] = poll_deliveries(first, 1)
    first.close()               # leaves the group without committing; a crashed worker leaves after its session timeout
    second = topic.consumer(group)
    [again] = poll_deliveries(second, 1)
    assert again == delivery
    second.commit(again)
    second.close()
    assert poll_after_assignment(topic.consumer(group)) == []


@needs_kafka
def test_a_rewind_delivers_the_same_message_again(topic):
    publisher = topic.publisher()
    assert publisher.publish(5) and publisher.publish(6)
    consumer = topic.consumer(topic.group())
    [first] = poll_deliveries(consumer, 1)
    consumer.rewind(first)
    assert [d.job_id() for d in poll_deliveries(consumer, 2)] == [5, 6]


# End to end: the job table, Kafka, workers and the reconciler

@pytest.fixture(params=BACKENDS)
def env(request, tmp_path):
    env = WorkerEnv(make_backend(request.param, tmp_path), tmp_path)
    yield env
    env.close()


def serve(env, worker, consumer, count, *, timeout=60.0):
    """worker handles deliveries until `count` more were handled, or until timeout."""
    target, deadline = len(env.handled) + count, time.monotonic() + timeout
    return worker.serve(consumer, stop=lambda: len(env.handled) >= target or time.monotonic() > deadline,

"""The systems extension's Compose services as seen from this machine: readiness, memory
peaks, and other projects' containers sharing Docker's VM (spec §11).

    uv run --group jobs python -m etf_risk.services ready mysql kafka
    uv run python -m etf_risk.services peaks mysql kafka
    uv run python -m etf_risk.services others --require-none

- ready waits until each service can do what the job system needs. MySQL: a login and
  SELECT 1, since the Compose healthcheck (mysqladmin ping) answers before logins work.
  Kafka: a metadata request that lists a broker. It exits 1 if a service is not ready
  within --timeout. The URLs come from ETF_RISK_MYSQL_URL and ETF_RISK_KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP,
  defaulting to the ports in docker/compose.yaml.
- peaks prints each service's cgroup v2 memory.peak, the highest usage since its container
  started (page cache included), against memory.max, the Compose limit, as docker/run.sh
  does for the pipeline container. A container that restarts may start a new count, so
  read peaks before a restart is injected.
- others counts the running containers that do not belong to this Compose project. It
  prints the count only, never their names: they use the same VM's memory, so memory
  budgets are measured with none running.

AI contribution: written with Claude Code (Opus 5.5). Tested with tests/test_services.py.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass

from etf_risk.provenance import REPO_ROOT

COMPOSE_FILE = REPO_ROOT / "docker" / "compose.yaml"
PROJECT = "etf-risk-jobs"                                   # the name: in docker/compose.yaml
SERVICES = ("mysql", "kafka")
DEFAULT_MYSQL_URL = "mysql://root:jobs-test@127.0.0.1:3307"   # compose.yaml's test password, 127.0.0.1 only
DEFAULT_KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP = "127.0.0.1:9094"


def _docker(*args: str, timeout: float = 60) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    return subprocess.run(["docker", *args], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Peak:
    service: str
    peak_bytes: int | None     # None: no memory.peak to read (the service is not running, or an older kernel)
    limit_bytes: int | None    # None: no limit ("max"), or unknown

    @property
    def fraction(self) -> float | None:
        return None if self.peak_bytes is None or not self.limit_bytes else self.peak_bytes / self.limit_bytes

    def describe(self) -> str:
        if self.peak_bytes is None:
            return f"{self.service}: memory.peak not available"
        text = f"{self.service}: memory.peak {self.peak_bytes / 2**20:,.0f} MiB"
        if self.limit_bytes:
            text += f" of {self.limit_bytes / 2**20:,.0f} MiB ({self.fraction:.0%})"
        return text + " (cgroup, includes page cache)"


def memory_peak(service: str) -> Peak:
    """The service container's memory.peak and memory.max (cgroup v2)."""
    out = _docker("compose", "-f", str(COMPOSE_FILE), "exec", "-T", service,
                  "cat", "/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.peak", "/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max")
    values = out.stdout.split()
    if out.returncode != 0 or len(values) != 2:
        return Peak(service, None, None)
    peak, limit = values
    return Peak(service, int(peak), None if limit == "max" else int(limit))

    out = _docker("ps", "--format", '{{.Label "com.docker.compose.project"}}')
    if out.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"docker ps failed with exit code {out.returncode}")
    return sum(1 for label in out.stdout.splitlines() if label.strip() != PROJECT)


def mysql_ready(url: str) -> None:
    from etf_risk.jobs.mysql import connect_mysql
    connection = connect_mysql(url)

    finally:

    metadata = AdminClient({"bootstrap.servers": bootstrap, "log_level": 0}).list_topics(timeout=5)
    if not metadata.brokers:
        raise RuntimeError("the metadata lists no broker")


def wait_until_ready(service: str, check: Callable[[], None], *, timeout: float, interval: float = 1.0,
                     clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic,
                     sleep: Callable[[float], None] = time.sleep) -> float:
    """Run check() until it returns; the seconds that took. TimeoutError, with the last
    error, once timeout has passed."""
    start = clock()
    while True:
        try:
            check()
            return clock() - start
        except Exception as error:
            last = error
        if clock() - start >= timeout:
            raise TimeoutError(f"{service} not ready after {timeout:g} s: {type(last).__name__}: {last}")
        sleep(interval)

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m etf_risk.services", description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    ready = commands.add_parser("ready", help="wait until each service can be used")
    ready.add_argument("services", nargs="+", choices=SERVICES)
    ready.add_argument("--timeout", type=float, default=120.0, help="seconds per service (default 120)")
    peaks = commands.add_parser("peaks", help="cgroup memory.peak against the limit")
    peaks.add_argument("services", nargs="+", choices=SERVICES)
    peaks.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="one JSON object per line")
    others = commands.add_parser("others", help="count containers outside this project")
    others.add_argument("--require-none", action="store_true", help="exit 1 if any is running")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    if args.command == "ready":
        checks = {"mysql": lambda: mysql_ready(os.environ.get("ETF_RISK_MYSQL_URL", DEFAULT_MYSQL_URL)),
                  "kafka": lambda: kafka_ready(os.environ.get("ETF_RISK_KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP", DEFAULT_KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP))}
        for service in args.services:
            try:
                seconds = wait_until_ready(service, checks[service], timeout=args.timeout)
            except TimeoutError as error:
                print(error, file=sys.stderr)
                return 1
            print(f"{service}: ready after {seconds:.1f} s")
        return 0
    if args.command == "peaks":
        for service in args.services:
            peak = memory_peak(service)
            print(json.dumps(asdict(peak)) if args.json else peak.describe())
        return 0
    count = other_containers()
    print(f"{count} running container(s) outside the {PROJECT} project")
    return 1 if args.require_none and count else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""etf_risk.services: memory peaks, the count of other projects' containers, and the
readiness wait, with a fake docker on PATH and a fake clock, so neither Docker nor a
service is needed.

AI contribution: written with Claude Code (Opus 5.5).
"""
import os

import pytest

from etf_risk import services

FAKE_DOCKER = r"""#!/bin/sh
# Answers the calls etf_risk.services makes, from FAKE_* variables.
case "$*" in
  *"exec -T mysql cat"*) printf '%s\n%s\n' "$FAKE_PEAK" "$FAKE_LIMIT" ;;
  *"exec -T kafka cat"*) echo "cat: /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.peak: No such file or directory" >&2
                         echo 671088640; exit 1 ;;
  "ps --format"*) printf '%s' "$FAKE_PS" ;;
  *) echo "unexpected call: $*" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
"""


@pytest.fixture
def fake_docker(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    bin_dir = tmp_path / "bin"
    bin_dir.mkdir()
    docker = bin_dir / "docker"
    docker.write_text(FAKE_DOCKER)
    docker.chmod(0o755)
    monkeypatch.setenv("PATH", f"{bin_dir}{os.pathsep}{os.environ['PATH']}")
    return monkeypatch


class FakeTime:
    def __init__(self):
        self.now = 0.0

    def clock(self):
        return self.now

    def sleep(self, seconds):
        self.now += seconds


def test_a_peak_is_read_with_its_limit(fake_docker, capsys):
    fake_docker.setenv("FAKE_PEAK", str(400 * 2**20))
    fake_docker.setenv("FAKE_LIMIT", str(512 * 2**20))
    peak = services.memory_peak("mysql")
    assert (peak.peak_bytes, peak.limit_bytes, peak.fraction) == (400 * 2**20, 512 * 2**20, 400 / 512)
    assert services.main(["peaks", "mysql"]) == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out == "mysql: memory.peak 400 MiB of 512 MiB (78%) (cgroup, includes page cache)\n"


def test_no_limit_and_a_missing_peak_are_reported_as_such(fake_docker, capsys):
    fake_docker.setenv("FAKE_PEAK", str(2**20))
    fake_docker.setenv("FAKE_LIMIT", "max")
    assert services.memory_peak("mysql") == services.Peak("mysql", 2**20, None)
    assert services.memory_peak("kafka") == services.Peak("kafka", None, None)
    assert services.main(["peaks", "kafka", "--json"]) == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out == '{"service": "kafka", "peak_bytes": null, "limit_bytes": null}\n'


def test_other_projects_are_counted_but_never_named(fake_docker, capsys):
    fake_docker.setenv("FAKE_PS", "etf-risk-jobs\nsomeone-elses-project\n\netf-risk-jobs\n")
    assert services.other_containers() == 2                  # a labelled one and one without a project
    assert services.main(["others", "--require-none"]) == 1
    out = capsys.readouterr()
    assert out.out == "2 running container(s) outside the etf-risk-jobs project\n"
    assert "someone-elses-project" not in out.out + out.err


def test_none_outside_the_project(fake_docker):
    fake_docker.setenv("FAKE_PS", "etf-risk-jobs\netf-risk-jobs\n")
    assert services.other_containers() == 0
    assert services.main(["others", "--require-none"]) == 0


def test_ready_retries_until_the_check_passes():
    fake, calls = FakeTime(), []

    def check():
        calls.append(fake.now)
        if len(calls) < 3:
            raise ConnectionRefusedError("refused")

    assert services.wait_until_ready("mysql", check, timeout=60, clock=fake.clock, sleep=fake.sleep) == 2.0
    assert calls == [0.0, 1.0, 2.0]


def test_ready_gives_up_after_the_timeout_with_the_last_error():
    fake = FakeTime()

    def check():
        raise ConnectionRefusedError(f"refused at {fake.now:g} s")

    with pytest.raises(TimeoutError, match=r"kafka not ready after 5 s: ConnectionRefusedError: refused at 5 s"):
        services.wait_until_ready("kafka", check, timeout=5, clock=fake.clock, sleep=fake.sleep)

import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass

from etf_risk.provenance import REPO_ROOT

COMPOSE_FILE = REPO_ROOT / "docker" / "compose.yaml"
PROJECT = "etf-risk-jobs"                                   # the name: in docker/compose.yaml
SERVICES = ("mysql", "kafka")
DEFAULT_MYSQL_URL = "mysql://root:jobs-test@127.0.0.1:3307"   # compose.yaml's test password, 127.0.0.1 only
DEFAULT_KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP = "127.0.0.1:9094"


def _docker(*args: str, timeout: float = 60) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    return subprocess.run(["docker", *args], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Peak:
    service: str
    peak_bytes: int | None     # None: no memory.peak to read (the service is not running, or an older kernel)
    limit_bytes: int | None    # None: no limit ("max"), or unknown

    @property
    def fraction(self) -> float | None:
        return None if self.peak_bytes is None or not self.limit_bytes else self.peak_bytes / self.limit_bytes

    def describe(self) -> str:
        if self.peak_bytes is None:
            return f"{self.service}: memory.peak not available"
        text = f"{self.service}: memory.peak {self.peak_bytes / 2**20:,.0f} MiB"
        if self.limit_bytes:
            text += f" of {self.limit_bytes / 2**20:,.0f} MiB ({self.fraction:.0%})"
        return text + " (cgroup, includes page cache)"


def memory_peak(service: str) -> Peak:
    """The service container's memory.peak and memory.max (cgroup v2)."""
    out = _docker("compose", "-f", str(COMPOSE_FILE), "exec", "-T", service,
                  "cat", "/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.peak", "/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max")
    values = out.stdout.split()
    if out.returncode != 0 or len(values) != 2:
        return Peak(service, None, None)
    peak, limit = values
    return Peak(service, int(peak), None if limit == "max" else int(limit))


def other_containers() -> int:
    """How many running containers belong to no service of this project: a count only."""
    out = _docker("ps", "--format", '{{.Label "com.docker.compose.project"}}')
    if out.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"docker ps failed with exit code {out.returncode}")
    return sum(1 for label in out.stdout.splitlines() if label.strip() != PROJECT)


def mysql_ready(url: str) -> None:
    from etf_risk.jobs.mysql import connect_mysql
    connection = connect_mysql(url)
    try:
        with connection.cursor() as cursor:
            cursor.execute("SELECT 1")
            if cursor.fetchone() != (1,):
                raise RuntimeError("SELECT 1 did not return 1")
    finally:
        connection.close()


def kafka_ready(bootstrap: str) -> None:
    from confluent_kafka.admin import AdminClient
    metadata = AdminClient({"bootstrap.servers": bootstrap, "log_level": 0}).list_topics(timeout=5)
    if not metadata.brokers:
        raise RuntimeError("the metadata lists no broker")


def wait_until_ready(service: str, check: Callable[[], None], *, timeout: float, interval: float = 1.0,
                     clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic,
                     sleep: Callable[[float], None] = time.sleep) -> float:
    """Run check() until it returns; the seconds that took. TimeoutError, with the last
    error, once timeout has passed."""
    start = clock()
    while True:
        try:
            check()
            return clock() - start
        except Exception as error:
            last = error
        if clock() - start >= timeout:
            raise TimeoutError(f"{service} not ready after {timeout:g} s: {type(last).__name__}: {last}")
        sleep(interval)


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m etf_risk.services", description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    ready = commands.add_parser("ready", help="wait until each service can be used")
    ready.add_argument("services", nargs="+", choices=SERVICES)
    ready.add_argument("--timeout", type=float, default=120.0, help="seconds per service (default 120)")
    peaks = commands.add_parser("peaks", help="cgroup memory.peak against the limit")
    peaks.add_argument("services", nargs="+", choices=SERVICES)
    peaks.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="one JSON object per line")
    others = commands.add_parser("others", help="count containers outside this project")
    others.add_argument("--require-none", action="store_true", help="exit 1 if any is running")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    if args.command == "ready":
        checks = {"mysql": lambda: mysql_ready(os.environ.get("ETF_RISK_MYSQL_URL", DEFAULT_MYSQL_URL)),
                  "kafka": lambda: kafka_ready(os.environ.get("ETF_RISK_KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP", DEFAULT_KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP))}
        for service in args.services:
            try:
                seconds = wait_until_ready(service, checks[service], timeout=args.timeout)
            except TimeoutError as error:
                print(error, file=sys.stderr)
                return 1
            print(f"{service}: ready after {seconds:.1f} s")
        return 0
    if args.command == "peaks":
        for service in args.services:
            peak = memory_peak(service)
            print(json.dumps(asdict(peak)) if args.json else peak.describe())
        return 0
    count = other_containers()
    print(f"{count} running container(s) outside the {PROJECT} project")
    return 1 if args.require_none and count else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

    uv run --group jobs python tests/mutation_check.py --list
    uv run --group jobs python tests/mutation_check.py --only renew-token rewind

Each mutation replaces one exact piece of source text, which must occur exactly once. The
work happens in a scratch copy of the repository (src/, tests/, pyproject.toml, uv.lock) with
its own environment (uv sync --frozen --group jobs), never in this checkout. The job tests
first run unmutated and must pass. Then, for each mutation, they run in a fresh process
group with a timeout:
- caught: pytest reports failing tests (exit 1);
- survived: they all pass (exit 0);
- error: any other exit, such as a collection error, or the timeout. A broken guard must
  fail a test, not hang one.

A mutation that needs a server is skipped unless its variable is set. The run exits 1 unless
every mutation that ran was caught. --out writes mutations.json, with this checkout's code
state, and the output tail of every run.

This list was rebuilt on 2026-10-23 from the descriptions of the earlier checks
(docs/job-table.md, docs/job-queue.md, the message of commit e2806bd). Those runs left no list
of their own, so it is not claimed to be the same set. Mutations that the remaining guards
make equivalent are left out; for example, mark_published's published_at condition is covered
by its version guard.

"""Mutation checks of the job queue's guards and settings: break one on purpose, run the job
tests, and expect them to fail (docs/job-table.md, docs/job-queue.md).

    uv run --group jobs python tests/mutation_check.py --out <folder>       # SQLite and offline Kafka settings
    ETF_RISK_MYSQL_URL=mysql://root:jobs-test@127.0.0.1:3307 ETF_RISK_KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP=127.0.0.1:9094 \\
        uv run --group jobs python tests/mutation_check.py --out <folder>   # also MySQL and Kafka
    uv run --group jobs python tests/mutation_check.py --list
    uv run --group jobs python tests/mutation_check.py --only renew-token rewind

Each mutation replaces one exact piece of source text, which must occur exactly once. The
work happens in a scratch copy of the repository (src/, tests/, pyproject.toml, uv.lock) with
its own environment (uv sync --frozen --group jobs), never in this checkout. The job tests
first run unmutated and must pass. Then, for each mutation, they run in a fresh process
group with a timeout:
- caught: pytest reports failing tests (exit 1);
- survived: they all pass (exit 0);
- error: any other exit, such as a collection error, or the timeout. A broken guard must
  fail a test, not hang one.

A mutation that needs a server is skipped unless its variable is set. The run exits 1 unless
every mutation that ran was caught. --out writes mutations.json, with this checkout's code
state, and the output tail of every run.

This list was rebuilt on 2026-10-23 from the descriptions of the earlier checks
(docs/job-table.md, docs/job-queue.md, the message of commit e2806bd). Those runs left no list
of their own, so it is not claimed to be the same set. Mutations that the remaining guards
make equivalent are left out; for example, mark_published's published_at condition is covered
by its version guard.

import shutil

from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO / "src"))
from etf_risk.provenance import code_state  # noqa: E402

STORE, WORKER, QUEUE = "src/etf_risk/jobs/store.py", "src/etf_risk/jobs/worker.py", "src/etf_risk/jobs/queue.py"
RECONCILER, KAFKA, MYSQL = "src/etf_risk/jobs/reconciler.py", "src/etf_risk/jobs/kafka.py", "src/etf_risk/jobs/mysql.py"

class Mutation:
    id: str
    file: str
    old: str
    new: str
    breaks: str
    needs: tuple[str, ...] = ()


def removing(id: str, file: str, context: str, piece: str, breaks: str, needs: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> Mutation:
    """Remove piece from context; context is what must occur exactly once in the file."""
    assert context.count(piece) == 1, (id, piece)
    return Mutation(id, file, context, context.replace(piece, "", 1), breaks, needs)


_RENEW = ("updated_at = :now\"\n                    \" WHERE job_id = :job_id AND status = 'running'"

_FAIL = ("'running' AND attempt_token = :token\",\n                    job_id=claim.job_id, token=claim.token,"

_REQUEUE = ("'running' AND attempt_token = :token\"\n                    \" AND lease_expires_at <= :now AND"

_EXHAUST = ("'running' AND attempt_token = :token\"\n                \" AND lease_expires_at <= :now AND"

    removing("accept-token", STORE, _ACCEPT, " AND attempt_token = :token", "acceptance without the token"),
    removing("fail-token", STORE, _FAIL, " AND attempt_token = :token", "fail_attempt without the token"),
    removing("takeover-lease", STORE, _TAKEOVER, " AND lease_expires_at <= :now", "a claim takes over a live lease"),
    Mutation("takeover-attempts-left", STORE, '" AND attempt_number < max_attempts", **take).rowcount:',

    removing("requeue-token", STORE, _REQUEUE, " AND attempt_token = :token", "the reconciler requeues on a stale token"),

    removing("exhaust-token", STORE, _EXHAUST, " AND attempt_token = :token", "exhausting a job on a stale token"),
    removing("claim-keeps-publication", STORE, _CLAIM, "published_at = NULL,", "a claim keeps the recorded publication"),
    removing("claim-version-bump", STORE, _CLAIM, "version = version + 1, ", "a claim does not bump the version"),
    removing("publication-version", STORE, "AND published_at IS NULL AND version = :version\",",

    Mutation("accept-repeat-token", STORE,

    Mutation("rollback", STORE, 'cursor.execute("ROLLBACK")', 'cursor.execute("COMMIT")',

    Mutation("one-row-check", STORE, "if count != 1:", "if count > 1:", "a job_attempts write may touch no row"),
    Mutation("conflict-detection", MYSQL, "error.args[0] in CONFLICT_ERRORS", "error.args[0] in ()",
             "deadlocks and lock wait timeouts are not run again", needs=("mysql",)),
    # The worker (docs/job-queue.md, "What the worker does with a delivery").
    Mutation("output-folder-check", WORKER, "exist_ok=False", "exist_ok=True", "an attempt writes into an existing folder"),
    Mutation("acknowledge-after-claim", WORKER, '        self._fault("after_claim")\n        acknowledge()\n',
             '        self._fault("after_claim")\n', "a claimed delivery is never acknowledged"),
    Mutation("rewind", WORKER, "consumer.rewind(delivery)", "pass", "a failed delivery is not read again"),
    Mutation("bounded-retries", WORKER, "if failures > retries:", "if False:", "serve() retries one message forever"),
    Mutation("malformed-commit", WORKER,
             "                served.malformed += 1\n                self._commit(consumer, delivery, served)\n",
             "                served.malformed += 1\n", "a malformed message is skipped without a commit"),
    # Job ids in messages (docs/job-queue.md, Settings).
    Mutation("job-id-leading-zero", QUEUE, 'rb"[1-9][0-9]{0,%d}"', 'rb"[0-9][0-9]{0,%d}"', "zero and leading zeros pass"),
    Mutation("job-id-format", QUEUE, "if _JOB_ID.fullmatch(self.value) is None:", "if False:", "text reaches int()"),
    Mutation("job-id-length", QUEUE, "MAX_JOB_ID_DIGITS - 1", "MAX_JOB_ID_DIGITS + 4999", "5,000 digits reach int()"),
    Mutation("job-id-range", QUEUE, "return job_id if job_id <= MAX_JOB_ID else None", "return job_id",

def make_scratch() -> Path:
    scratch = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="etf-risk-mutations-"))
    ignore = shutil.ignore_patterns("__pycache__", ".pytest_cache")
    for item in COPIED:
        source = REPO / item
        if source.is_dir():
            shutil.copytree(source, scratch / item, ignore=ignore)
        else:
            shutil.copy2(source, scratch / item)
    env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k != "VIRTUAL_ENV"}
    subprocess.run(["uv", "sync", "--frozen", "--group", "jobs"], cwd=scratch, env=env, check=True,
                   capture_output=True, text=True)
    return scratch


def run_tests(scratch: Path, timeout: float) -> dict:
    """The job tests in a new process group; the group is killed on timeout."""
    env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k != "VIRTUAL_ENV"}
    command = [str(scratch / ".venv" / "bin" / "python"), "-m", "pytest", *JOB_TESTS, "-x", "-q",
               "-p", "no:cacheprovider"]
    start = time.monotonic()
    process = subprocess.Popen(command, cwd=scratch, env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                               text=True, start_new_session=True)
    try:
        output, _ = process.communicate(timeout=timeout)
        code = process.returncode
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
        output, _ = process.communicate()
        code = None
    failed = next((line for line in output.splitlines() if line.startswith("FAILED ")), None)
    return {"exit_code": code, "seconds": round(time.monotonic() - start, 1), "first_failure": failed,
            "output_tail": output[-3000:]}


def outcome(result: dict) -> str:
    return {1: "caught", 0: "survived"}.get(result["exit_code"], "error")


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--only", nargs="+", metavar="ID", help="run these mutations only")
    parser.add_argument("--timeout", type=float, default=600.0, help="seconds per run of the job tests (default 600)")
    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, help="folder for mutations.json")
    parser.add_argument("--list", action="store_true", help="list the mutations and exit")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.list:
        for m in MUTATIONS:
            print(f"{m.id:26} {m.file.removeprefix('src/etf_risk/jobs/'):14} {m.breaks}"
                  + (f"  (needs {', '.join(m.needs)})" if m.needs else ""))
        return 0
    unknown = set(args.only or ()) - {m.id for m in MUTATIONS}
    if unknown:
        parser.error(f"unknown mutation(s): {', '.join(sorted(unknown))}")
    selected = [m for m in MUTATIONS if not args.only or m.id in args.only]
    backends = {name: bool(os.environ.get(variable)) for name, variable in NEEDS.items()}
    record = {"format": 1, "started_at_utc": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(), "code": code_state(),
              "backends": {"sqlite": True, **backends}, "timeout_s": args.timeout, "mutations": []}
    scratch = make_scratch()
    try:
        baseline = run_tests(scratch, args.timeout)
        record["baseline"] = baseline
        print(f"baseline: exit {baseline['exit_code']} in {baseline['seconds']} s")
        if baseline["exit_code"] != 0:
            print(baseline["output_tail"], file=sys.stderr)
            print("the unmutated job tests must pass first", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        for m in selected:
            missing = [need for need in m.needs if not backends[need]]
            if missing:
                record["mutations"].append({**asdict(m), "outcome": "skipped", "missing": missing})
                print(f"skipped   {m.id} (needs {', '.join(missing)})")
                continue
            path = scratch / m.file
            original = path.read_text()
            if original.count(m.old) != 1:
                raise SystemExit(f"{m.id}: the text to replace occurs {original.count(m.old)} times in {m.file}")
            path.write_text(original.replace(m.old, m.new, 1))
            try:
                result = run_tests(scratch, args.timeout)
            finally:
                path.write_text(original)
            record["mutations"].append({**asdict(m), "outcome": outcome(result), **result})
            print(f"{outcome(result):9} {m.id} ({result['seconds']} s){'  ' + result['first_failure'] if result['first_failure'] else ''}")
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(scratch, ignore_errors=True)
    ran = [m for m in record["mutations"] if m["outcome"] != "skipped"]
    record["summary"] = {o: sum(1 for m in record["mutations"] if m["outcome"] == o)
                         for o in ("caught", "survived", "error", "skipped")}
    print(f"{record['summary']['caught']} of {len(ran)} caught; {record['summary']}")
    if args.out:
        args.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (args.out / "mutations.json").write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + "\n")
    return 0 if ran and all(m["outcome"] == "caught" for m in ran) else 1

content.content:
## claim(): two guarded updates

A claim tries two conditional updates of the job's row, in one transaction:

```sql
-- 1. a queued job
UPDATE jobs SET status = 'running', attempt_number = attempt_number + 1, attempt_token = :token,
       lease_expires_at = :lease_expires_at, version = version + 1, updated_at = :now
 WHERE job_id = :job_id AND status = 'queued';
-- 2. only if 1 matched no row: a running job whose lease has expired, with attempts left
UPDATE jobs SET ... (the same)
 WHERE job_id = :job_id AND status = 'running' AND lease_expires_at <= :now
   AND attempt_number < max_attempts;
```

## Transactions

- Every operation is one transaction. Apart from `submit`, each writes both tables: the
  update of `jobs` decides, and the write to `job_attempts` records; that write must touch
  exactly one row, or the store raises and both tables roll back.
- Any exception rolls the transaction back, including a simulated crash. The tests raise at
  each gap between two statements (`FAULT_POINTS`) and check both tables afterwards.
- Every transaction locks the `jobs` row before any `job_attempts` row, and none spans a
  pipeline run: locks last milliseconds, and a crashed worker leaves an expiring lease, not a
  held lock.
- A COMMIT that fails may still have taken effect, so repeating an operation must be safe:
  `accept_result` returns true when the accepted attempt's token is the caller's.
- In MySQL, an operation rolled back by a deadlock or a lock wait timeout runs again, up to
  three runs in all.

## What is checked where

- [`tests/test_jobs_store.py`](../tests/test_jobs_store.py) and
  [`tests/test_jobs_worker.py`](../tests/test_jobs_worker.py) run on SQLite, and on MySQL as

# Job table: claims, tokens and transactions

How the job store ([`src/etf_risk/jobs/store.py`](../src/etf_risk/jobs/store.py)) keeps the
guarantee of [spec §11](spec.md): each job accepts at most one result, and every succeeded
job has exactly one accepted result. A job may execute more than once. The example follows
two workers, A and B, and job 7, with a lease of 60 seconds. How jobs reach the workers
through Kafka, and how the reconciler requeues and republishes them, is in
[job-queue.md](job-queue.md).

## claim(): two guarded updates

A claim tries two conditional updates of the job's row, in one transaction:

```sql
-- 1. a queued job
UPDATE jobs SET status = 'running', attempt_number = attempt_number + 1, attempt_token = :token,
       lease_expires_at = :lease_expires_at, version = version + 1, updated_at = :now
 WHERE job_id = :job_id AND status = 'queued';
-- 2. only if 1 matched no row: a running job whose lease has expired, with attempts left
UPDATE jobs SET ... (the same)
 WHERE job_id = :job_id AND status = 'running' AND lease_expires_at <= :now
   AND attempt_number < max_attempts;
```

The WHERE clause is the guard; the number of rows matched is the answer. If one update matched,
the same transaction reads the new attempt number, marks the previous attempt `expired` (after
a takeover only), and inserts the new attempt's row: its token, its run id `job-7-attempt-<n>`
and its output folder. If neither matched, a read only says why (finished, lease held, not
found). The one write that can follow, failing a job whose last attempt's lease expired,
carries its own guard on the token that read saw.

## Token checks

Renewal, acceptance and failure all use the same guard:

```sql
UPDATE jobs SET ... WHERE job_id = :job_id AND status = 'running' AND attempt_token = :token;
```

There is no time in it: a token holds until a claim replaces it, and an update that matches no
row means the worker has been fenced off. Acceptance sets `succeeded`, a terminal status, and
clears the token, so no token matches afterwards: at most one result is accepted. A CHECK
constraint ties `accepted_attempt` to `succeeded`, so a succeeded job names exactly one.

## Two workers, one job

| Time | Worker A | Worker B | Job 7 afterwards |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 s | claim: update 1 matches; attempt 1, token tA, lease until 60 s | | running, attempt 1, tA |
| 5 s | | a duplicate delivery; claim: neither update matches, refused (lease held) | unchanged |
| 10 s | renew with tA: lease until 70 s | | running, attempt 1, tA |
| 10–75 s | stalls, no heartbeat | | |
| 75 s | | claim: update 2 matches (70 ≤ 75); attempt 2, token tB; attempt 1 marked expired | running, attempt 2, tB |
| 80 s | renew with tA: no row matches, so A is fenced off and stops | | unchanged |
| 90 s | | accept with tB: succeeded, accepted attempt 2 | succeeded |
| 95 s | had A not stopped, accept with tA: no row matches, and the accepted attempt's token is tB, so false | | unchanged |

Job 7 executed twice, in `job-7-attempt-1` and `job-7-attempt-2`, and accepted one result. Had
nobody claimed it at 75 s, A's renewal at 80 s would have matched, since tA would still be
current, and A could have finished: the lease decides only when a takeover may happen.

If A and B claim queued job 7 at the same instant, both updates target the same row. In
MySQL, InnoDB lets the first lock the row and makes the second wait; when the first commits,
the waiting update reads the row as committed, not as an earlier snapshot of its own, finds
it running, and matches nothing. Update 2 matches nothing either, since the new lease is
live, so B is refused. In SQLite, `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` takes a write lock on the whole database,

row first decides, and the other then finds the job succeeded, or a token that is not its own.

- In MySQL, an operation rolled back by a deadlock or a lock wait timeout runs again, up to

```sql
       lease_expires_at = :lease_expires_at, published_at = NULL, version = version + 1, updated_at = :now
 WHERE job_id = :job_id AND status = 'queued';
-- 2. only if 1 matched no row: a running job whose lease has expired, with attempts left
UPDATE jobs SET ... (the same)
 WHERE job_id = :job_id AND status = 'running' AND lease_expires_at <= :now
   AND attempt_number < max_attempts;
```

The WHERE clause is the guard; the number of rows matched is the answer. If one update matched,
the same transaction reads the new attempt number, marks the previous attempt `expired` (after
a takeover only), and inserts the new attempt's row: its token, its run id `job-7-attempt-<n>`
and its output folder. If neither matched, a read only says why (finished, lease held, not
found). The one write that can follow, failing a job whose last attempt's lease expired,
carries its own guard on the token that read saw.

## Token checks

Renewal, acceptance and failure all use the same guard:

```sql
UPDATE jobs SET ... WHERE job_id = :job_id AND status = 'running' AND attempt_token = :token;
```

There is no time in it: a token holds until a claim replaces it, and an update that matches no
row means the worker has been fenced off. Acceptance sets `succeeded`, a terminal status, and
clears the token, so no token matches afterwards: at most one result is accepted. A CHECK
constraint ties `accepted_attempt` to `succeeded`, so a succeeded job names exactly one.

## Two workers, one job

| Time | Worker A | Worker B | Job 7 afterwards |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 s | claim: update 1 matches; attempt 1, token tA, lease until 60 s | | running, attempt 1, tA |
| 5 s | | a duplicate delivery; claim: neither update matches, refused (lease held) | unchanged |
| 10 s | renew with tA: lease until 70 s | | running, attempt 1, tA |
| 10–75 s | stalls, no heartbeat | | |
| 75 s | | claim: update 2 matches (70 ≤ 75); attempt 2, token tB; attempt 1 marked expired | running, attempt 2, tB |
| 80 s | renew with tA: no row matches, so A is fenced off and stops | | unchanged |
| 90 s | | accept with tB: succeeded, accepted attempt 2 | succeeded |
| 95 s | had A not stopped, accept with tA: no row matches, and the accepted attempt's token is tB, so false | | unchanged |

Job 7 executed twice, in `job-7-attempt-1` and `job-7-attempt-2`, and accepted one result. Had
nobody claimed it at 75 s, A's renewal at 80 s would have matched, since tA would still be
current, and A could have finished: the lease decides only when a takeover may happen.

## At the same moment

If A and B claim queued job 7 at the same instant, both updates target the same row. In
MySQL, InnoDB lets the first lock the row and makes the second wait; when the first commits,
the waiting update reads the row as committed, not as an earlier snapshot of its own, finds
it running, and matches nothing. Update 2 matches nothing either, since the new lease is
live, so B is refused. In SQLite, `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` takes a write lock on the whole database,
so B's transaction starts only after A's has committed: the same outcome, for another reason.
Likewise when A accepts while B takes over an expired lease: whichever transaction holds the
row first decides, and the other then finds the job succeeded, or a token that is not its own.

## Transactions

- Every operation is one transaction. Apart from `submit` and `mark_published`, each writes
  both tables: the update of `jobs` decides, and the write to `job_attempts` records; that
  write must touch exactly one row, or the store raises and both tables roll back.
- Any exception rolls the transaction back, including a simulated crash. The tests raise at
  each gap between two statements (`FAULT_POINTS`) and check both tables afterwards.
- Every transaction locks the `jobs` row before any `job_attempts` row, and none spans a
  pipeline run: locks last milliseconds, and a crashed worker leaves an expiring lease, not a
  held lock.
- A COMMIT that fails may still have taken effect, so repeating an operation must be safe:
  `accept_result` returns true when the accepted attempt's token is the caller's.
- In MySQL, an operation rolled back by a deadlock or a lock wait timeout runs again, up to
  three runs in all.

## What is checked where

- [`tests/test_jobs_store.py`](../tests/test_jobs_store.py) and
  [`tests/test_jobs_worker.py`](../tests/test_jobs_worker.py) run on SQLite, and on MySQL as
  well when `ETF_RISK_MYSQL_URL` is set. On SQLite, competing connections run one after another
  under the database lock: those runs check the state logic, not InnoDB's row locks.
- [`tests/test_jobs_mysql.py`](../tests/test_jobs_mysql.py) checks the MySQL adapter offline
  and, against a server, the InnoDB behaviour the SQL relies on (setup in its docstring and in
  [`docker/compose.yaml`](../docker/compose.yaml)).
- Status on 2026-10-22: with MySQL 8.4.13 from the Compose file and `ETF_RISK_MYSQL_URL` set,
  all 222 cases pass, in five runs in a row; without the URL, 114 pass and the 7 tests that
  need a server are skipped. Breaking any one of eleven guards and checks on purpose (the
  token, lease and attempts-left conditions, the rollback, the one-row check on
  `job_attempts` writes, the `version` bump, conflict detection, the output folder check)
  makes at least one test fail. On top of main at e55f76b (after the caching experiment),
  the job tests give the same counts and the whole suite passes (350 passed, 7 skipped).
  The MySQL container's memory peak in a full run was 339 MiB of its 512 MiB budget
  (cgroup `memory.peak`, which includes page cache).

## What the worker does with a delivery
## What is checked where

- [`tests/test_jobs_reconciler.py`](../tests/test_jobs_reconciler.py) and
  [`tests/test_jobs_queue.py`](../tests/test_jobs_queue.py) use the in-memory queue. They
  run on SQLite, and on MySQL as well when `ETF_RISK_MYSQL_URL` is set. They cover:
  - the guards and the grace period;
  - the job-id format, including a 5,000-digit payload and ids beyond the range, each
    followed by a valid job that must still run;
  - the worker's commits, rewinds and bounded retries;
  - whole scenarios, including a seeded run with lost publications and crashes at every
    fault point.
  Tests that run a loop (`serve()`, the reconciler's `run()`) stop it themselves, after a
  number of tries or a few seconds, so a broken guard makes them fail rather than hang.
- [`tests/test_jobs_kafka.py`](../tests/test_jobs_kafka.py) checks the settings offline.
  With `ETF_RISK_KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP` set, it checks against Kafka 4.3.1 from
  [`docker/compose.yaml`](../docker/compose.yaml):
  - delivery to a fresh consumer group, and `latest` for comparison;
  - confirmation, including an unreachable broker;
  - commits and rewinds;
  - a 5,000-digit payload ahead of a job: both committed, and the job runs;
  - a message left uncommitted after the retries, for a restarted worker;
  - two end-to-end scenarios.
- Status on 2026-10-23:
  - **Offline:** 200 passed, and the 17 tests that need MySQL, Kafka or confluent-kafka
    were skipped.
  - **With Kafka 4.3.1** (the job table on SQLite): 210 passed, and the 7 tests that
    need MySQL were skipped.
  - **With MySQL 8.4.13 and Kafka 4.3.1, on the committed revision e2806bd:** 379
    passed, none failed or skipped, in one run on fresh containers (162 cases on each
    store). An earlier revision, before the job-id validation, had 353 passed.
  - **The whole suite:** 411 passed and 15 skipped. That run came before the bounded
    retries, the job-id validation and the test fixes; the rest of the suite does not
    use these files.
  - **Mutation checks:** 22 guards and settings were broken on purpose, one at a time,
    in 25 test runs: three were run both offline and against Kafka. Each run had a
    timeout. The 22 include 4 for the job-id format and range. Tests failed in all 25
    runs; none ran into the timeout. Before the fixes, three ran until it:
    - a claim that keeps the publication, through `serve()`'s unbounded retries;
    - the grace boundary off by one, through a test that waited for the publisher to
      stop the reconciler's loop;
    - the rewind removed, through a test that waited for a failing claim to come back.
  - **Memory:** spec §11 records the peaks. MySQL reached 511 of its 512 MiB over about
    two hours of repeated runs, and 472 MiB after two runs on a fresh container. That
    is limited headroom, not evidence that longer runs stay within the limit.

input.new_string:
in the container (a Linux VM on macOS, data on bind mounts) are a separate
configuration, not comparable with native measurements.

### Systems extension services (runbook)

These are for the optional job queue ([spec §11](docs/spec.md)).
- **Compose services.** MySQL and Kafka run in Docker Compose
  ([docker/compose.yaml](docker/compose.yaml)), each with a memory limit and reachable from
  this machine only.
- **Clients.** The job package's clients, PyMySQL and confluent-kafka, are pinned in the
  `jobs` dependency group.
- **Git worktrees.** In a worktree, `data/` is a symlink to the main checkout's (ignored by
  Git): `ln -s <main checkout>/data data`.

```bash
docker compose -f docker/compose.yaml up -d --wait mysql kafka
# The healthchecks only see open ports; this waits for a MySQL login and SELECT 1, and Kafka metadata
uv run --group jobs python -m etf_risk.services ready mysql kafka
# The job tests against both services (offline, they run on SQLite and skip these)
ETF_RISK_MYSQL_URL=mysql://root:jobs-test@127.0.0.1:3307 ETF_RISK_KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP=127.0.0.1:9094 \
    uv run --group jobs python -m pytest tests/test_jobs_*.py
# Each container's cgroup memory.peak against its limit, and the containers of other projects (a count)
uv run python -m etf_risk.services peaks mysql kafka
uv run python -m etf_risk.services others
# Break each guard on purpose and expect a failing test; set the two variables to include MySQL and Kafka
uv run --group jobs python tests/mutation_check.py --out data/outputs-mutations
docker compose -f docker/compose.yaml down -v      # removes the data volumes as well
```

- **Memory budgets** (spec §11) are measured with no other project's containers in Docker's
  VM; `services others --require-none` exits 1 otherwise.
- **Still to come.** The worker, reconciler and submit commands, with the real pipeline, and
  the Redis result cache are added in later milestones. Until then, the worker runs only the
  simulated pipeline, inside the tests.

def test_a_stale_token_is_refused_on_the_last_attempt_too(env):
    """The same on the path that fails a job. The reconciler read A's token, B took the job
    over on its last attempt, and B's lease expired as well. Without the token guard in the
    update that exhausts a job, A's stale token would fail the job through B's attempt."""
    job, a = lapsed(env, max_attempts=2)
    lease = env.admin.expired_leases()[0]                                       # A's token
    b = env.admin.claim(job, "worker-B", env.runs)                              # a takeover: attempt 2 of 2
    env.clock.advance(LEASE.total_seconds())                                    # B's lease expires too
    before = env.dump()
    assert env.admin.requeue_expired(lease.job_id, lease.token) is None
    assert env.dump() == before
    assert env.admin.requeue_expired(job, b.token) is Status.FAILED             # B's own token: none left

# Job table: claims, tokens and transactions

How the job store ([`src/etf_risk/jobs/store.py`](../src/etf_risk/jobs/store.py)) keeps the
guarantee of [spec §11](spec.md): each job accepts at most one result, and every succeeded
job has exactly one accepted result. A job may execute more than once. The example follows
two workers, A and B, and job 7, with a lease of 60 seconds. How jobs reach the workers
through Kafka, and how the reconciler requeues and republishes them, is in
[job-queue.md](job-queue.md).

## claim(): two guarded updates

A claim tries two conditional updates of the job's row, in one transaction:

```sql
-- 1. a queued job
UPDATE jobs SET status = 'running', attempt_number = attempt_number + 1, attempt_token = :token,
       lease_expires_at = :lease_expires_at, published_at = NULL, version = version + 1, updated_at = :now
 WHERE job_id = :job_id AND status = 'queued';
-- 2. only if 1 matched no row: a running job whose lease has expired, with attempts left
UPDATE jobs SET ... (the same)
 WHERE job_id = :job_id AND status = 'running' AND lease_expires_at <= :now
   AND attempt_number < max_attempts;
```

The WHERE clause is the guard; the number of rows matched is the answer. If one update matched,
the same transaction reads the new attempt number, marks the previous attempt `expired` (after
a takeover only), and inserts the new attempt's row: its token, its run id `job-7-attempt-<n>`
and its output folder. If neither matched, a read only says why (finished, lease held, not
found). The one write that can follow, failing a job whose last attempt's lease expired,
carries its own guard on the token that read saw.

## Token checks

Renewal, acceptance and failure all use the same guard:

```sql
UPDATE jobs SET ... WHERE job_id = :job_id AND status = 'running' AND attempt_token = :token;
```

There is no time in it: a token holds until a claim replaces it, and an update that matches no
row means the worker has been fenced off. Acceptance sets `succeeded`, a terminal status, and
clears the token, so no token matches afterwards: at most one result is accepted. A CHECK
constraint ties `accepted_attempt` to `succeeded`, so a succeeded job names exactly one.

## Two workers, one job

| Time | Worker A | Worker B | Job 7 afterwards |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 s | claim: update 1 matches; attempt 1, token tA, lease until 60 s | | running, attempt 1, tA |
| 5 s | | a duplicate delivery; claim: neither update matches, refused (lease held) | unchanged |
| 10 s | renew with tA: lease until 70 s | | running, attempt 1, tA |
| 10–75 s | stalls, no heartbeat | | |
| 75 s | | claim: update 2 matches (70 ≤ 75); attempt 2, token tB; attempt 1 marked expired | running, attempt 2, tB |
| 80 s | renew with tA: no row matches, so A is fenced off and stops | | unchanged |
| 90 s | | accept with tB: succeeded, accepted attempt 2 | succeeded |
| 95 s | had A not stopped, accept with tA: no row matches, and the accepted attempt's token is tB, so false | | unchanged |

Job 7 executed twice, in `job-7-attempt-1` and `job-7-attempt-2`, and accepted one result. Had
nobody claimed it at 75 s, A's renewal at 80 s would have matched, since tA would still be
current, and A could have finished: the lease decides only when a takeover may happen.

## At the same moment

If A and B claim queued job 7 at the same instant, both updates target the same row. In
MySQL, InnoDB lets the first lock the row and makes the second wait; when the first commits,
the waiting update reads the row as committed, not as an earlier snapshot of its own, finds
it running, and matches nothing. Update 2 matches nothing either, since the new lease is
live, so B is refused. In SQLite, `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` takes a write lock on the whole database,
so B's transaction starts only after A's has committed: the same outcome, for another reason.
Likewise when A accepts while B takes over an expired lease: whichever transaction holds the
row first decides, and the other then finds the job succeeded, or a token that is not its own.

## Transactions

- Every operation is one transaction. Apart from `submit` and `mark_published`, each writes
  both tables: the update of `jobs` decides, and the write to `job_attempts` records; that
  write must touch exactly one row, or the store raises and both tables roll back.
- Any exception rolls the transaction back, including a simulated crash. The tests raise at
  each gap between two statements (`FAULT_POINTS`) and check both tables afterwards.
- Every transaction locks the `jobs` row before any `job_attempts` row, and none spans a
  pipeline run: locks last milliseconds, and a crashed worker leaves an expiring lease, not a
  held lock.
- A COMMIT that fails may still have taken effect, so repeating an operation must be safe:
  `accept_result` returns true when the accepted attempt's token is the caller's.
- In MySQL, an operation rolled back by a deadlock or a lock wait timeout runs again, up to
  three runs in all.

## What is checked where

- [`tests/test_jobs_store.py`](../tests/test_jobs_store.py) and
  [`tests/test_jobs_worker.py`](../tests/test_jobs_worker.py) run on SQLite, and on MySQL as
  well when `ETF_RISK_MYSQL_URL` is set. On SQLite, competing connections run one after another
  under the database lock: those runs check the state logic, not InnoDB's row locks.
- [`tests/test_jobs_mysql.py`](../tests/test_jobs_mysql.py) checks the MySQL adapter offline
  and, against a server, the InnoDB behaviour the SQL relies on (setup in its docstring and in
  [`docker/compose.yaml`](../docker/compose.yaml)).
- [`tests/mutation_check.py`](../tests/mutation_check.py) breaks the guards and checks on
  purpose, one at a time, in a scratch copy of the repository, and expects the job tests to
  fail within a timeout. It covers the token, lease and attempts-left conditions, the
  rollback, the one-row check on `job_attempts` writes, the `version` bump, conflict
  detection, the output folder check, and the queue's guards in
  [job-queue.md](job-queue.md).
- Status when this table was merged (PR #7), on 2026-10-22:
  - with MySQL 8.4.13 from the Compose file and `ETF_RISK_MYSQL_URL` set, all 222 cases
    passed, in five runs in a row;
  - without the URL, 114 passed and the 7 tests that need a server were skipped;
  - breaking any one of eleven guards and checks by hand made at least one test fail.
    Those mutations were not recorded as a list; `tests/mutation_check.py` rebuilds them
    from this description;
  - the MySQL container's memory peak in a full run was 339 MiB of its 512 MiB budget
    (cgroup `memory.peak`, which includes page cache).

  The current status of the job tests, with the Kafka delivery of PR #8, is in
  [job-queue.md](job-queue.md).

*AI contribution: written with Claude Code (Opus 5.5).*

**What changed**
- **`74c8481` Provenance and dependencies.**

  - `etf_risk.services` waits until MySQL accepts a login and Kafka answers, reads each container's peak memory, and counts other projects' containers without naming them.
  - `tests/mutation_check.py` breaks each of 31 guards and settings on purpose and expects a failing test.
